data.title: S1. Company and actor directory
data.summary: A guided tour of the 97 companies and organisations in companies.csv, grouped by what they do, with location, scale signal, status and sources, followed by a dated timeline of Vietnamese alternative protein from 2015 to September 2026.
data.body:
# S1. Company and actor directory

This appendix is a narrative guide to `companies.csv` (97 rows). It groups the actors by what they contribute to supply: making non-animal protein foods, making or importing protein ingredients, buying protein for feed, financing, and supporting the field. Each group has a compact table. The appendix ends with a dated timeline built from `timeline.csv` and wave 2 verification.

How to read the tables:

- **Location** is the current (post-1 July 2025) province, with the former unit in brackets where it changed. See [[app-s10-admin-map]].
- **Scale signal** is the best published indicator we found. "Claimed" means a company or press statement not checked against a filing. "Design capacity" is what a plant was built for, not what it makes.
- **Status** gives the last evidence of activity and the date of our last check. "Wave 1" rows were checked on 23 September 2026 by the ecosystem research; "wave 2" rows were re-checked the same day by a separate verification pass, which used direct page reads only. Many company sites failed to load in wave 2, so many rows carry only wave 1 evidence.
- **Sources** resolve in `sources.csv`. Where wave 2 changed a wave 1 value, the change is recorded in the `change_log` column of `companies.csv` and flagged below as a correction.

> **Method note.** The directory is broad but not complete. The wave 1 web-search budget ran out part way through (the ecosystem research logged about 40 searches and 60 page reads), and wave 2 used no web search at all (see the working papers and [[app-m1-method]]). Entities we could not confirm are kept and marked "lead" or "unverified". Absence of an actor here means "not found", not "does not exist".

## S1.1 Overview

- **Vietnam's real non-animal protein economy is incumbent, not startup.** Soy milk (Vinasoy and the dairy majors) and industrial *đồ chay* (traditional vegetarian food made by meat and frozen-food processors and by specialist SMEs) are the scale players [@ECO-41; @ECO-40] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Modern plant-based startups are few and very small**, and we found no disclosed institutional equity round for any Vietnamese plant-based food startup [@ECO-13; @CAP-15] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **The largest alternative-protein production asset is insect meal** (Entobel, about 11,000 t a year design capacity, the sum of two plants, our calculation) [@ECO-02; @ECO-03] {VN-direct|High}. We treat insects as a benchmark, not a recommended play.
- **Chinese fermentation by-product protein is already sold into Vietnamese feed** by a local distributor [@ECO-69] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **We found no cultivated meat or seafood company or facility in Vietnam.** The only links we found are Vietnamese corporate stakes abroad and one memorandum with no follow-up found [@ECO-58; @VCO-22] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **GFI's global company database lists 2 Vietnamese companies**, both plant-based, founded in 2019 and 2023, and no Vietnamese research actors [@VCO-21] {VN-direct|Medium}.

Rows by category in `companies.csv`: plant-based meat 18, traditional chay industrial 18, other (buyers, investors, support) 15, plant-based dairy 10, distributor 9, feed SCP or yeast 6, microalgae 5, cultivated 4, ingredient supplier 3, fermentation biomass 2, duckweed 2, insect (benchmark) 2, mushroom or mycelium 1, plant-based seafood 1 (our count of `companies.csv`; that one row, Bien Phuong, makes meat substitutes on its sources, as shown below). The groups below regroup these rows by supply role and add actors found in the retail audit ([[app-s2-retail-audit]]).

## S1.2 Incumbent soy and dairy

| Name | Location | What they do | Scale signal | Status, last verified | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vinasoy (Vietnam Soymilk Company, unit of Quang Ngai Sugar JSC, QNS) | Quang Ngai; plants in Bac Ninh (Tien Son Industrial Park) and Ho Chi Minh City (VSIP 2A, former Binh Duong) | Fami and Vinasoy soy milks; Veyo nut milks | Soy-milk revenue above VND 4,100 bn in 2024 (about USD 158 million at VND 26,000 per USD, our calculation), about 80% of soy milk, gross margin above 39%; 390 million L a year in three plants (2022) | Active. 2025 capacity not found in wave 2 | [@ECO-41; @ECO-42; @IND-48; @IND-49; @IND-50; @VCO-17; @FTR-16] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Vinamilk (plant-based lines) | Ho Chi Minh City | Nut, oat and soy milks (some blended with fresh milk), pea-protein "high-protein" milk, plant yoghurt, plant creamer | 17 SKU rows in the retail audit; nut milk reported "double-digit growth" in Q1 2026 (no figure) | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-43; @ECO-44; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| TH Group (TH true NUT) | Nghe An (farm) | Walnut, macadamia and almond milks with dates (oat as an ingredient); walnut variant contains fresh cow milk | Launched 17 March 2018; walnut variant 1 g protein per 100 ml | Active (wave 1); a hybrid, not fully plant-based | [@ECO-45; @ECO-40] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Nutifood (plant milks) | Ho Chi Minh City | Brown rice and corn milks | On shelf at VND 24,800 (6 Sep 2026) | Field observation only | [@ECO-40] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| ToFu House | Hung Yen (Van Giang) | Industrial tofu; pilot domestic soybean fields | Capacity of 150 to 500 t of tofu a month (2023); ISO 22000 | Active as of 2023 | [@FORM-36; @IND-51] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| My Hoa tofu-skin craft village | Vinh Long (former Binh Minh town, former Vinh Long province) | *Tàu hũ ky* (tofu skin) from mainly imported soybeans | 27 households, over 200 workers, about 7 t a day | National intangible heritage (2022) | [@FORM-14] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Tofu brands on shelf (Song Long, Pulmuone, Tafu, Ichiban) | not verified | Fresh tofu | One or two SKU rows each | On shelf September 2026 | [@FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Low} |

Readings. Vinasoy is the largest soy-milk maker in Vietnam, and it runs on imported soybeans [@ECO-41] {VN-direct|Medium}. The soy-milk share figures are company or press-reported, not audited: 82.7% (December 2014) and about 80% (2024) [@ECO-42; @ECO-41] {VN-direct|Medium}. TH true NUT and several Vinamilk products blend plant and dairy, which blurs the boundary of "plant-based" [@ECO-45; @ECO-43] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S1.3 Industrial chay makers

These firms make *đồ chay* at industrial scale. Label evidence splits their products into two types: vegetable-filler chay (dumplings, spring rolls: mostly jicama, taro, mung bean and mushroom, with little protein) and protein-analogue chay (mock meats, canned slices: soy protein, TVP, tofu skin and wheat gluten) [@ECO-33; @FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. We found no manufacturer that publishes chay tonnage (our search) [@ECO-25; @IND-53] {VN-direct|Medium}.

| Name | Location | What they do | Scale signal | Status, last verified | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VISSAN (Vietnam Livestock Technology JSC) | Ho Chi Minh City (420 No Trang Long, former Binh Thanh district) | Meat processor with 8 chay SKUs, including chay dumplings and wontons launched 27 August 2026; canned chay slices | Whole-company 2026 target of 20,350 t processed food (all lines) | Active (wave 2). SATRA 67.8%, Masan MEATLife 24.9% (2025 annual report); UPCoM VSN since October 2016 | [@ECO-30; @ECO-31; @VCO-13; @BUY-04] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| CJ Foods Vietnam (Cau Tre, bibigo) | Plants reported in Ho Chi Minh City (former Ba Ria-Vung Tau) and Tay Ninh (former Long An) | Chay spring rolls, dumplings, bibigo Healthy Mandu chay | 20 of 186 SKU rows in the audit; volumes not disclosed | Active. Business unit of CJ CheilJedang (South Korea); CJ in Vietnam since 1999. Cau Tre acquisition year and plant list not verified in wave 2 | [@ECO-34; @FORM-24; @VCO-12; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| SG Food (Saigon Food JSC) | Ho Chi Minh City (Vinh Loc Industrial Park, former Binh Chanh district) | Frozen ready meals and seafood; chay fried rice, chay hotpot kit | Exports to Japan | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-29; @FORM-31] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Au Lac (Au Lac Vegan Food Trade and Manufacture Co., Ltd) | Ho Chi Minh City (735-737 Nguyen Kiem, former Go Vap; a site at Thoi An ward, former District 12, is also recorded) | Seven chay categories on the English page (spices, instant, sterilised, canned, frozen, dry, beverages); eight on the Vietnamese page, adding baked goods | Exports claimed to USA, Canada, Australia, Germany, UK; Halal, ISO 9001 and 22000, FSSC 22000 claimed; one audited SKU at 25.1 g protein per 100 g | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-26; @FORM-20; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Thoai An Trading Co., Ltd | Ho Chi Minh City (Tan Tao Industrial Park, former Binh Tan district) | Tofu-skin rolls, chay sausages, chay seafood (shrimp cake, "seafood tofu") | Founded 2005; HACCP; nationwide distribution claimed | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-27; @FORM-26] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| An Nhien Foods (Pham Gia Phat Trading and Import-Export Co., Ltd) | Ho Chi Minh City (Hiep Thanh ward, former District 12) | Soy and barley TVP chay meats, dried slices, frozen meals | 12 SKU rows, the broadest modern-chay range in the audit; brand from late 2014; Halal; exports claimed to Korea, Europe, North America | Active (wave 2). Registered as a trader; no factory or capacity disclosed | [@VCO-26; @ECO-28; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| GN Foods JSC | Tay Ninh (former Long An): Long Hau Extended Industrial Park, Can Giuoc commune | Frozen Vietnamese foods; co-packer of a Co.op Select chay line | Founded 2009; 2,000 staff; factory 20,415 m2, processing plant 35,107 m2; BRCGS, ISO 22000, HACCP, Halal, BAP | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-35; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Cholimex Food JSC | Ho Chi Minh City (Vinh Loc Industrial Park, former Binh Chanh district) | Sauces and seasonings including chay kits; frozen spring rolls, dumplings and buns (bun filling with soy flour and chay ribs) | Chay bun label 5.74 g protein per 100 g | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-37; @FORM-27; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| LC Foods JSC | Ho Chi Minh City (Rach Bap Industrial Park, Tay Nam ward, former Binh Duong) | Chay spring rolls using TVP granules 4-7 mm | Tax code 3702777811 | Found in the retail audit; registry look-up failed in wave 2 | [@FORM-28] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Agrex Saigon Foodstuffs JSC (Top V, AS Food) | Ho Chi Minh City (former District 7) | Export dumplings and dim sum, including one chay mushroom dumpling | Volumes not disclosed | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-36] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Thanh Dung (Thuc pham chay Thanh Dung) | Ho Chi Minh City (Thuan An, former Binh Duong) | Chay maker listing TVP among products; raw materials imported from USA, Australia and Canada | Tax code 3702548219; founded 2009 | Company site only; whether it extrudes or repacks TVP is unknown | [@FORM-35] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Xuan Hong (dried chay slices brand) | not identified | Dried soy and gluten slices | One SKU at 65.2 g protein per 100 g dry | Owner and plant unknown; brand site unreachable | [@FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Directory-only SMEs: Vegan 24H, Happy Farm, Vuong Ngoc Vegan | Hanoi; Ho Chi Minh City; Tay Ninh | Mock meats, tofu products, dried chay foods | Directory listings only | Not verified | [@ECO-38] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Other chay brands on shelf: P.G.P, Vifon (chay noodles), Saky Foods, MANI, Hue One Food, Song Huong Foods | various | Chay cakes, noodles, pastries, buns, frozen chay sausages and fish cakes | One or two SKU rows each | Owners mostly not verified; P.G.P not identified | [@FORM-01; @ECO-40] {VN-direct\|Low} |

> **Correction.** The wave 1 ecosystem directory listed LC Foods as a lead "not found" (row CO-046). The retail audit found LC Foods JSC with a product page naming TVP granules and a plant in Rach Bap Industrial Park, Ho Chi Minh City (former Binh Duong) [@FORM-28] {VN-direct|High}. The same company page gives its tax code, 3702777811 [@FORM-28] {VN-direct|Medium}; a registry look-up in wave 2 failed. The directory row should be read with this correction.

> **Correction.** A prior lead named "Xuan Hong" as an industrial chay maker. The Xuan Hong found by the ecosystem research is a cassava starch processor in Tay Ninh (former Tay Ninh), with a capacity of 100 t of starch a day (2020); police recorded a violation in December 2020 for bypassing wastewater treatment [@ECO-39] {VN-direct|Medium}. A different "Xuan Hong" dried-slice brand is on shelf, owner not identified [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Low}. The two should not be merged (logged in [[app-r2-disagreements]]).

Readings:

- **Meat processors are the scale chay makers.** VISSAN, CJ Foods Vietnam, Cholimex and SG Food sell chay in the same frozen categories as meat [@IND-53; @FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. They are the most plausible co-packers for new plant-based products, with GN Foods for retailer private labels.
- **The protein-dense specialists are in Ho Chi Minh City** (An Nhien, Au Lac, Thoai An; the Xuan Hong brand's location is not verified) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. They are the natural first customers for a domestic TVP or gluten substitute ([[app-s2-retail-audit]], section S2.13).
- **Many small makers exist beyond the brands seen.** A 2022 to 2023 food-safety survey covered 126 vegetarian food production, processing and trading establishments in Hanoi alone [@FORM-37] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S1.4 Modern plant-based brands made in Vietnam

| Name | Location | What they do | Scale signal | Status, last verified | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cay De Food Company (VMEAT) | Ho Chi Minh City (assumed) | Plant-based burger patties, mince, *chả lụa*, ham | VND 3 bn invested from 2018; retail VND 164,000 to 445,000 per kg (2022) | No evidence after 2022 | [@ECO-17; @ECO-19] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Bien Phuong | not known | Plant-based meat substitutes | Entered mid-2020 | No evidence after 2022 | [@ECO-17; @ECO-19] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| NutriGreen Food JSC | Ho Chi Minh City (former District 10) | Plant-based meat substitutes (soy, rice, coconut) | No scale data | Website did not resolve on 23 Sep 2026 | [@ECO-25] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Vinamit JSC (jackfruit "vegan meat") | Ho Chi Minh City (not verified) | Young-jackfruit meat for export; a low-protein texturiser (our inference) | No volume found | Corporate active; jackfruit line status unknown | [@ECO-17; @ECO-18] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Is It Meat? | Ho Chi Minh City | Nuggets, sausages, schnitzels for restaurants | Sold via restaurants (2022) | Unknown; single blog source | [@ECO-15] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Yukino Foods | Ho Chi Minh City (Thao Dien) | Gyoza, falafel, burgers | One shop plus online (2022) | Unknown; claims unverified | [@ECO-15] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Kashew Cheese | Ho Chi Minh City | Fermented cashew cheeses, yoghurt, milk | Founded 2020; several deli cafes; 3 SKU rows in the audit | Active (wave 1) | [@ECO-49; @ECO-50; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Deep Blue Island | not verified | Cultured cashew and coconut products | 5 SKU rows in Ho Chi Minh City premium stores | Brand domain redirects to an unrelated site; owner not verified | [@FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Two unnamed firms in the GFI database | not known | One plant-based dairy (cheese), one meat or seafood plus ingredients | Founded 2019 and 2023 | Names not rendered; neither founding year matches Emmay or Kashew | [@VCO-21] {VN-direct\|Medium} |

We found no Vietnamese plant-based egg product; a 2022 list of 12 brands includes none [@ECO-15] {VN-direct|Low}. The only plant-protein fundraising found is Emmay's (section S1.6). Press estimates of the Vietnamese plant-based meat market ("about VND 1,000 bn" in 2022; "USD 500 million within several years" in 2024) give no traceable basis and are not used [@ECO-17; @ECO-18] {VN-direct|Low}.

## S1.5 Imported brands and their channels

Imported "modern" brands entered mostly through restaurants and gourmet shops; some also reached AEON Citi Mart and K-Market. Importers distribute some brands (Classic Fine Foods for Next Meats), but we found no national distributor for any of them [@ECO-15; @ECO-16] {VN-direct|Medium}. Mintel's database logged no plant-based meat launches in Vietnam from 2022 to Q2 2023 [@ECO-23] {VN-direct|High}.

**Brands**

| Brand (origin) | Vietnam entry and channel | Scale or price signal | Status, last verified | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Beyond Meat (USA) | August 2019 at BiaCraft (3 Ho Chi Minh City venues); later gourmet retail and e-commerce | VND 1.2 to 1.8 million per kg (2022) | Present via importers in 2022; current availability unverified | [@ECO-16; @ECO-19] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| OmniFoods (Hong Kong) | Gourmet retail by 2022; Starbucks Vietnam menu in summer 2023 | Limited-time menu | Last Vietnam evidence 2023; brand site did not resolve on 23 Sep 2026 | [@ECO-15; @ECO-20] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Heura (Spain), Next Meats (Japan), CK Foods (Taiwan), Verdino (probably Romania) | Gourmet retailers, AEON Citi Mart, K-Market and Classic Food Deli (2022) | Next Meats VND 52,000 per 80 g (2022) | Unknown in 2026; single blog source | [@ECO-15; @ECO-19] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Unconventional (Italy) | Ho Chi Minh City premium stores | 2 SKU rows: burger and sausage, 15 to 16 g protein, SPC and SPI | On shelf 16 Sep 2026 | [@FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Ong Cha Va / NOSAFOOD | Co.opmart and Emart canned aisles; labelled "Plant Based" at Co.opmart Nha Trang | About VND 70,000 per 200 g at Co.opmart Nha Trang, about 3 to 3.3 times VISSAN's canned chay per 100 g; VND 76,000 per 200 g at Emart | On shelf September 2026; origin disputed (China or Vietnam) | [@ECO-40; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| 137 Degrees (Simple Foods, Thailand) | Nha Trang supermarkets and a Ho Chi Minh City specialty grocer | 9 SKU rows; about VND 93,000 to 158,900 per pack | On shelf September 2026 | [@ECO-46; @FORM-01; @FORM-38] {VN-adjacent\|Medium} |
| Oatside (Singapore brand, made in Bandung, Indonesia) | Launched in Ho Chi Minh City November to December 2022 | 3 SKU rows | Active; marketing backlash April 2026 | [@ECO-47; @ECO-48] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Oatly (Sweden), MilkLab and Alternative Dairy Co (Australia), Almond Breeze (USA), So Good | Specialty and mainstream supermarkets | 1 to 4 SKU rows each | On shelf September 2026 | [@FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Dairy-Free Down Under (Australia) | Annam Gourmet, Nam An, The Food Shop (2022) | n/a | Unknown in 2026 | [@ECO-15] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| INNOHAS (South Korea) | VinaCapital Ventures investment (July 2024) to enter Vietnam | Undisclosed | No Vietnam launch found; company site does not mention Vietnam (23 Sep 2026) | [@ECO-65; @VCO-31] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Impossible Foods, Zhenmeat | No evidence of a Vietnam launch | n/a | Absence of evidence only (our search) | none (our search) {general\|Low} |
| Nestle Harvest Gourmet | No evidence of Vietnam sale | n/a | harvestgourmet.com redirects to a domain-for-sale page (23 Sep 2026) | [@VCO-25] {general\|Low} |

> **Correction.** The wave 1 directory could not identify "Unconventional" (row CO-018). The Ho Chi Minh City retail audit found two Unconventional SKUs, labelled as made in Italy and built on SPC, SPI and textured soy [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. The owner is believed to be Gruppo Veronesi (not verified). It is the only extruded "modern" analogue on the shelves we saw.

**Channels, importers and retailer private labels**

| Name | Location | Role | Status, last verified | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BiaCraft | Ho Chi Minh City | Craft beer bars; says it was the first to serve Beyond Burger in Vietnam (August 2019) | Unknown in 2026 | [@ECO-16] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Starbucks Vietnam | Ho Chi Minh City | Ran OmniFoods items in summer 2023 | Promotion ended (assumed) | [@ECO-20] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| SaladStop! Vietnam | Ho Chi Minh City | Plant-based patties in a salad chain (2022) | Unknown | [@ECO-15] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Annam Gourmet; Nam An Market | Ho Chi Minh City | Gourmet importer-retailers; 11 and 26 SKU rows in the audit; most imported at Nam An (20 of 26), 4 of 11 at Annam | Active retailers (audit, 16 Sep 2026) | [@ECO-15; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Classic Fine Foods Vietnam (Classic Food Deli) | not stated | Official distributor of Next Meats, sold online via Classic Food Deli (2022) | Unknown for alt protein | [@ECO-15] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Bewina | Ho Chi Minh City | Importer of plant-based sausages and mince | Unknown; brand origin (Romania) given only by ECO-19 | [@ECO-17; @ECO-19] {VN-direct\|Low} |
| Saigon Co.op (Co.op Select) | Ho Chi Minh City | Private-label chay dumplings, buns, spring rolls, gyoza-noodle meal; 12 SKU rows | On shelf September 2026 | [@FORM-01; @FORM-29; @FORM-30] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Lotte Mart Vietnam (Choice L) | Ho Chi Minh City | Private-label chay spring rolls and dumplings; maker not identified | On shelf September 2026 | [@ECO-40; @FORM-01] {VN-direct\|Medium} |

## S1.6 Mushroom, mycelium and tempeh

## S1.14 Timeline of key events, 2015 to September 2026

Events come from `timeline.csv` (48 rows) and wave 2 verification. Dates are as reported; "c." means approximate. Before 2015 the incumbents built the base: spirulina at Vinh Hao (site chosen 1976), CJ's entry into Vietnamese food (1999), Thoai An (2005), Vinasoy's Bac Ninh phase 1 (90 million L a year, May 2013) and An Nhien's brand (2014) [@ECO-52; @ECO-34; @ECO-27; @ECO-42; @ECO-28] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**2015**
- August 2015: Vinasoy completes Bac Ninh phase 2, reaching 180 million L a year there after more than VND 1,280 bn of investment [@ECO-42] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**2016 to 2018**
- c. 2016: Cricket One starts; its farms are in Loc Ninh, Dong Nai (former Binh Phuoc) [@ECO-11] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 2016: Yukino Foods claims to be the first plant-based meat brand in Vietnam (single blog claim) [@ECO-15] {VN-direct|Low}.
- 2017: Emmay formalised as a company in Ho Chi Minh City; VAST transfers spirulina technology to VN Vastcom (Nghe An) [@ECO-13; @ECO-53] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 2018: Cay De starts VMEAT plant-based meat R&D (VND 3 bn invested in 2018; about two years of R&D) [@ECO-17; @ECO-19] {VN-direct|Low}.
- 17 March 2018: TH launches TH true NUT (with fresh cow milk) [@ECO-45] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**2019**
- 2019: Entobel's first Vietnamese plant (Dong Nai, 1,000 t a year of insect meal) operating [@ECO-02; @ECO-03] {VN-direct|High}.
- June 2019: OmniPork's Asian roadmap excludes Vietnam [@ECO-21] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 17 August 2019: BiaCraft introduces the Beyond Burger in three Ho Chi Minh City venues [@ECO-16] {VN-direct|Medium}.

- 1 October 2025: Royal De Heus announces the purchase of CJ Feed & Care (17 mills in five countries) [@VCO-07] {VN-direct|High}.
- 14 October 2025: Decree 264/2025/ND-CP on national and local venture funds takes effect [@CAP-29] {VN-direct|High}.
- 26 November 2025: Skretting Vietnam and Entobel partnership; first commercial insect-meal shrimp feed in Vietnam (company claim) [@VCO-28] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 10 December 2025 (reported): VAL's second crushing line takes capacity to 2.6 Mt of soybeans a year [@VCO-16] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**2026**
- Q1 2026: Vinamilk reports double-digit growth in nut milk (no figure) [@ECO-44] {VN-direct|Low}.
- 3 March 2026: De Heus completes the CJ Feed & Care purchase [@VCO-08] {VN-direct|High}.
- 5 March 2026: Ho Chi Minh City launches its VND 500 bn venture fund [@CAP-32] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 30 March to 4 April 2026: Oatside's Vietnam "Chief Milk Officer" campaign draws backlash [@ECO-48] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 22 April 2026: Hanoi Venture Capital Fund established [@CAP-35] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 22 July 2026: De Heus opens a marine and cold-water fish feed mill in Vinh Long, 168,000 t a year design capacity (84,000 t in trade press) [@VCO-10; @IND-45] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- 27 August 2026: VISSAN launches chay dumplings and wontons [@ECO-30] {VN-direct|High}.
- 6, 16 and 20 September 2026: AltProtein Vietnam retail audit in Nha Trang and Ho Chi Minh City: large frozen chay sections, no modern branded meat analogues in mass retail, Chinese-labelled canned "Plant Based" soy luncheon meat on shelf [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## Gaps and how to close them

| Gap | Cheapest way to close it |
|---|---|
| Chay tonnage and protein inputs by manufacturer | Call VISSAN, CJ Foods Vietnam, SG Food, Au Lac, Thoai An and GN Foods; check the NSO enterprise census for the relevant product codes. |
| CJ's Cau Tre acquisition year and CJ Foods Vietnam plant list | CJ CheilJedang disclosures on DART; Cau Tre shareholder filings; CJ Foods Vietnam annual or sustainability report. |
| The names of GFI's 2 Vietnamese companies | Email GFI APAC or download the database spreadsheet. |
| Cricket One status in 2025 and 2026 | Dong Nai business registry, LinkedIn, or a phone call. |
| Chinese single-cell protein import volumes and makers | Customs data for HS 2309 and 2102; call CK Vietnam / V-Group. |
| Skretting's H-Meal inclusion rate and volumes | Ask Skretting Vietnam or Entobel. |
| Which Vietnamese mills came with CJ Feed & Care | Ask De Heus Vietnam communications. |
| Spirulina output and producers' status | Phone checks; MAE or provincial statistics. |
| NGO, association and event ecosystem (HSI, ProVeg, vegetarian associations, expos, university contests) | A new search round with web access. |
| Unverified leads (Song Huong Foods, Hue One Food, Tan Nhat Huong, Deep Blue Island, Hat Viet, Vinaorganic, Tan Huu Qui) | One call or registry look-up each. |
| Owner of the Xuan Hong dried-slice brand and the Ong Cha Va / NOSAFOOD origin | Read the manufacturer and origin lines on the packs. |

See also [[app-r1-open-questions]].

## Related data files

- `companies.csv`: 97 companies and organisations (including Thai Duong Feed), with `change_log` for wave 2 corrections and `last_verified` dates.
- `timeline.csv`: 48 dated events (1976 to September 2026).
- `brands.csv`: 53 brands from the retail audit, with owner, manufacturer and plant location.
- `ingredient_suppliers.csv`: 22 ingredient supply rows (trade flows, distributors, processors).
- `deals.csv` and `investors.csv`: financing events and investors ([[app-s11-capital]]).
- `facilities.csv`: plants, mills and fermentation capacity ([[app-s5-facilities]]).
- Working papers: `working-papers/wave1/ecosystem/` and `working-papers/wave2/verify_co/`.

data.title: S2. Retail formulation audit (Nha Trang and Ho Chi Minh City, September 2026)
data.summary: What 186 plant-protein products on 11 Vietnamese shelves are made of, who makes them and where their protein comes from. Most of the shelf is low in protein, every protein-dense local product runs on imported soy protein or wheat gluten, and no Vietnamese textured soy protein plant was found.
data.body:
# S2. Retail formulation audit (Nha Trang and Ho Chi Minh City, September 2026)

This appendix reads the retail shelf as supply-side evidence. A product label tells us which protein ingredient a Vietnamese manufacturer buys, who made the product, where the plant is, and how much protein reaches the consumer. We use the shelf to map ingredient demand and manufacturers, not to size a consumer market.

The audit covered every non-animal protein product we could find in 11 modern and specialty stores: traditional Vietnamese vegetarian food, *đồ chay* (mock meats, filled wrappers and ready meals), tofu, plant milks and yoghurts, vegan cheese, imported "modern" meat analogues and protein powders. The field data are cited as [@FORM-01]. Trade figures, company facts and ingredient channels are cited to their own sources.

Terms used in this appendix:

- **TVP**: textured vegetable (soy) protein, made by extrusion.
- **SPC**: soy protein concentrate. **SPI**: soy protein isolate, the more refined, higher-protein form.
- *đạm đậu nành* (soy protein): the label term used for TVP, SPC and SPI alike. Labels rarely say which.
- *tàu hũ ky* (tofu skin, yuba). *mì căn* (wheat gluten, seitan).
- **Hydrated**: sold wet (ready-to-cook or ready-to-eat). **Dry**: sold dried, for example dried TVP slices.
- **SKU row**: one product in one store. The same product seen in three stores is three SKU rows but one **unique product**.

## S2.1 Key findings

1. **Most of the plant-protein shelf is not a protein product.** Plant milks (51 SKU rows, 27%) and filled wrappers such as spring rolls, dumplings and buns (47 rows, 25%) are the two largest groups among 186 SKU rows [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. Across 43 unique hydrated foods with a label value, median protein is 4.7 g per 100 g; 53% have under 5 g and 16% reach 10 g [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
2. **Chay has two protein tiers with little in between.** Filled wrappers with mung bean fillings carry 1.5 to 5.7 g protein per 100 g (median 4.0 g, 14 products). Gluten or TVP analogues carry 12 to 25 g hydrated (median 19 g, 5 products), and dried TVP or gluten slices 53 to 67 g as sold (median 64 g, 5 products) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
3. **Every locally made product with 10 g or more protein per 100 g runs on an imported protein ingredient.** All 10 such unique products (8 An Nhien, 1 Xuan Hong, 1 Au Lac) use (or, for three, almost certainly use) soy protein, TVP, SPC or wheat gluten. Local foods with no imported protein ingredient reach at most 4.6 g (median 3.0 g, n = 8) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
4. **About 77 to 88% of SKU rows depend on an imported main protein ingredient.** Of 170 SKU rows where the main protein ingredient could be identified, 77% rely on an imported one, 11% partly and 12% on a domestic one [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
5. **China is a major supplier of concentrated plant-protein ingredients.** China reported exports to Vietnam in 2023 of 7,957 t of protein concentrates and textured protein (HS 2106.10), 10,028 t of HS 3504 (which includes SPI) and 10,338 t of wheat gluten [@FORM-05; @FORM-06; @FORM-07] {VN-direct|High}.
6. **We found no commercial TVP extrusion in Vietnam.** Distributors sell Chinese SPI and gluten in 20 to 25 kg bags; one An Nhien label names soy protein from Serbia (logged as SPC); Chinese extrusion lines are offered for sale [@FORM-11; @FORM-12; @FORM-01; @FORM-34] {VN-direct|Medium}. This is absence of evidence after a limited search.
7. **Protein is cheapest in the least processed soy and wheat formats.** Median price per 100 g of protein: tofu VND 66,265; dried TVP slices VND 64,584; hydrated gluten or TVP analogues VND 111,585; filled wrappers VND 368,798; cashew cheese VND 875,797 [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
8. **The only "modern" SPC or SPI analogues are imported and cost about five times more per gram of protein** than local gluten or TVP analogues (VND 542,424 to 621,528 against a median of VND 111,585 per 100 g of protein) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
9. **The mainstream frozen chay shelf is split between Vietnamese firms and Korean-owned CJ Foods Vietnam**, which accounts for 20 of 186 SKU rows through Cau Tre and bibigo [@FORM-01; @FORM-24] {VN-direct|Medium}. Imported finished products (40 rows) sit mostly in premium stores [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
10. **The natural first customers for a domestic protein ingredient are a short, Ho Chi Minh City-based list:** An Nhien, Au Lac, Xuan Hong (location not verified), LC Foods, Cholimex, CJ Foods Vietnam, VISSAN, Thoai An, and co-packers such as GN Foods (section S2.13).

## S2.2 Method

### Stores, dates and collector

One field collector working for AltProtein Vietnam visited 11 stores on three days: five in Nha Trang (Khanh Hoa) on 6 September 2026, two in Ho Chi Minh City on 16 September 2026 and four in Ho Chi Minh City on 20 September 2026 [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. The collector photographed shelves, price tags and packs, then filled ingredients and nutrition from pack photos or, where the pack was not legible, from the brand's own page or a retailer listing ("collector OSINT", with the link logged per row).

| Store | City | Date | Channel | Price positioning | SKU rows | Imported finished rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lotte Mart Nha Trang | Nha Trang | 6 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 13 | 0 |
| Co.opmart Nha Trang | Nha Trang | 6 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 25 | 3 |
| GO! Nha Trang | Nha Trang | 6 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 26 | 3 |
| Moonmilk Super Market Nha Trang | Nha Trang | 6 Sep 2026 | specialty retail | premium | 9 | 8 |
| WinMart Nha Trang (Vincom Le Thanh Ton) | Nha Trang | 6 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 11 | 2 |
| Annam Gourmet An Phu | Ho Chi Minh City | 16 Sep 2026 | specialty retail | premium | 11 | 4 |
| Nam An Market, 21 Thao Dien | Ho Chi Minh City | 16 Sep 2026 | specialty retail | premium | 26 | 20 |
| Co.opmart Nguyen Kiem | Ho Chi Minh City | 20 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 48 | 0 |
| GO! Nguyen Kiem | Ho Chi Minh City | 20 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 6 | 0 |
| Emart Phan Van Tri | Ho Chi Minh City | 20 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed to premium | 7 | 0 |
| Lotte Mart Go Vap | Ho Chi Minh City | 20 Sep 2026 | modern retail | mixed | 4 | 0 |
| **Total** | | | | | **186** | **40** |

Source for the table: [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. "Imported finished rows" counts rows logged as imported, plus the five Nha Trang rows of 137 Degrees (a Thai brand logged as local in Nha Trang and reclassified; see [[app-r2-disagreements]]), minus one An Nhien row packed in Vietnam from an imported ingredient. Store addresses in the store log are approximate for four Nha Trang stores (map pins, not captured on site).

### What was recorded

The product log has 23 fields per SKU row: store, product name, brand, origin, category, format, pack size, shelf price, price per 100 g, a conventional equivalent price where logged, shelf placement, ingredients, and five nutrition values per 100 g or 100 ml (energy, protein, fat, carbohydrate, sodium) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. The cleaned file `retail_audit_skus.csv` has 46 fields. It keeps the logged values and adds derived fields such as product type, as-sold form, formulation archetype, primary and secondary protein sources, a non-vegan flag, price per 100 g of protein, an import flag, brand owner, manufacturer, plant location and confidence.

Coverage of the key fields [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}:

- 120 SKU rows have an ingredient list.
- 78 SKU rows (66 unique products) have a protein value.
- Price confidence: High for 125 rows (clear shelf tag), Medium for 27 rows (online reference price, not shelf), Low for 34 rows (shared shelf tags, unclear multipacks, one outlier).
- Row confidence (`data_confidence`): High 82, Medium 39, Low 65.

### Derived prices

Price per 100 g (or 100 ml) is the shelf price divided by pack size. Price per 100 g of protein is price per 100 g divided by (protein g per 100 g / 100). All prices are in VND at the shelf, including promotions where the tag showed one. Where we give USD, we convert at VND 26,000 per USD (our calculation).

> **Method note.** SKU rows are facings on a shelf, not sales. Shares in this appendix are shares of observed products, not of volume or value. Protein statistics use unique products (one value per product). Price statistics use SKU rows, because the same product has different prices in different stores. Product-type labels in the data files use the US spelling "analog"; the text uses "analogue".

## S2.3 Sample structure

| Product type | SKU rows | Nha Trang | Ho Chi Minh City | As sold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plant milk | 51 | 33 | 18 | beverage |
| dumpling, spring roll or bun with vegetable filling | 47 | 23 | 24 | ready-to-cook |
| frozen meat or seafood analogue | 21 | 7 | 14 | 9 ready-to-cook, 12 ready-to-eat |
| canned analogue | 9 | 5 | 4 | ready-to-eat |
| vegan cheese or spread | 9 | 0 | 9 | ready-to-eat |
| other (instant noodles, falafel, nutritional yeast, pesto, condensed coconut milk) | 9 | 5 | 4 | mixed |
| dried TVP or soy chunks | 8 | 2 | 6 | dry |
| plant yoghurt or creamer | 8 | 3 | 5 | ready-to-eat |
| tofu | 8 | 3 | 5 | ready-to-cook |
| ready meal | 7 | 3 | 4 | mixed |
| snack or jerky (mushroom jerky) | 5 | 0 | 5 | dry |
| protein powder | 4 | 0 | 4 | dry |
| **Total** | **186** | **84** | **102** | |

Source: [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. Ho Chi Minh City premium stores contributed every vegan cheese, protein powder and mushroom jerky row.

**Primary protein source.** The main protein ingredient named on the label (or inferred where the label lists it first among protein ingredients) groups as follows [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}:

| Primary protein source | SKU rows | Where it appears |
|---|---|---|
| soy protein, TVP, SPC or SPI | 28 | canned analogues, dried slices, mandu, seafood-style analogues, imported burger |
| soybean, tofu or soy milk | 26 | soy milks, tofu, seafood tofu |
| mung bean (*đậu xanh*) | 19 | spring rolls and dumplings (CJ, VISSAN, Cholimex, Co.op Select, LC Foods) |
| oat | 19 | oat milks, oat yoghurt |
| unknown | 18 | unbranded or unpublished private-label rows |
| other nuts (almond, walnut, macadamia, pistachio) | 17 | nut milks |
| wheat flour (bun dough or wrapper) | 13 | steamed buns, wonton, samosa, gyoza-noodle meal |
| wheat gluten or wheat protein | 8 | An Nhien fish and meat analogues, Thoai An crab stick and *chả lụa* (pork-roll style) |
| rice or corn | 8 | rice milk, corn milk, fried rice, rice noodles |
| mushroom | 7 | mushroom jerky (5), one frozen analogue, one dumpling |
| cashew | 7 | cultured cashew cheeses |
| pea protein | 7 | high-protein milks, yoghurts, powders |
| chickpea, hemp, none, other | 9 | falafel, hummus, powders, spreads |

**Ingredient frequency.** Among the 120 rows with an ingredient list: mushroom appears in 42 rows (27 products), soy protein or TVP wording in 31 (23), soybean, tofu or soy milk in 29 (25), mung bean in 25 (16), oat in 16 (12), wheat gluten in 9 (9), tofu skin in 9 (6), pea protein in 7 (5) and cashew in 5 (5) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. Mushroom is the most common ingredient but is used for texture and flavour, not protein.

## S2.4 Classification rules

Every SKU row was classified by hand, with a note wherever a judgement was made [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.

- **Product type** (12 types, table S2.3) and **as-sold form** (beverage, ready-to-cook, ready-to-eat, dry).
- **Formulation archetype** (A0 to A15, section S2.6): a code for what the product is made of and how its protein is delivered. A0 marks rows that are not protein products or lack data.
- **Primary protein family**: the ingredient that supplies most of the protein, judged from label order and percentages.
- **Import flag** (`likely_imported_protein_ingredient`). *Y* if the main protein ingredient is soy protein, soybean, tofu, soy milk, tofu skin, wheat gluten or flour, pea, oat, almond or another imported nut, chickpea or hemp, or if the product is an imported finished good. *Partial* if a domestic protein ingredient such as mung bean shares the role with an imported one. *N* if the main protein is mung bean, rice, corn, coconut or vegetables. The flag is inferred from ingredient type, not traced to a supplier.
- **Non-vegan flag**: EGG or DAIRY where the label lists them. Five rows carry the flag: egg noodles in two Co.op Select vegetarian gyoza-noodle rows, skim milk powder in Thoai An *chả lụa ớt xiêm chay*, fresh cow milk in TH true NUT walnut, and one unconfirmed TH true NUT row [@FORM-01; @FORM-26] {VN-direct|High}. *Chay* (vegetarian in the Buddhist sense) is therefore not the same as *thuần chay* (strictly vegan).
- **Brand normalisation.** For example "Cau Tre (CJ Cau Tre)" became "Cau Tre (CJ Foods Vietnam)", and one Veyo row attributed to Nutifood was corrected to Vinasoy, because Quang Ngai Sugar (QNS) lists VEYO as its nut-milk brand [@FORM-33] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Protein values.** Values written as a regulatory minimum ("≥3.5", quoted by a price site) were excluded (1 row). Where the same product carried a label value elsewhere in the audit, that value was borrowed and flagged (8 rows in the cleaned file).
- **Translation.** "Wheat starch" on two An Nhien analogues with 18.8 to 19.7 g protein is almost certainly gluten (*bột mì căn*) and was treated as gluten [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Outlier.** A Vinamilk plant yoghurt at VND 10,000 for 4 x 100 g was excluded from price statistics [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.

## S2.5 Protein by product type

Protein content by product type and form, unique products with a label value, g per 100 g or 100 ml [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}:

| Product type (form) | n | Median | Range |
|---|---|---|---|
| dried TVP or soy chunks (dry) | 5 | 64.0 | 53.3 to 66.7 |
| protein powder (dry, all imported) | 4 | 47.0 | 41.2 to 58.3 |
| frozen analogue, ready-to-eat | 4 | 19.3 | 3.0 to 25.1 |
| frozen analogue, ready-to-cook | 5 | 15.0 | 3.03 to 19.0 |
| other, ready-to-cook (falafel) | 2 | 9.0 | 9.0 |
| vegan cheese or spread | 2 | 8.9 | 8.03 to 9.7 |
| canned analogue | 2 | 6.8 | 4.5 to 9.08 |
| tofu | 5 | 5.0 | 3.8 to 9.3 |
| filled wrappers (dumpling, spring roll, bun) | 18 | 4.3 | 1.53 to 6.3 |
| ready meal (one ready-to-cook, one ready-to-eat) | 2 | 4.2 | 4.2 |
| plant yoghurt or creamer | 3 | 1.9 | 1.6 to 2.93 |
| plant milk (per 100 ml) | 14 | 1.6 | 0.7 to 5.0 |

Readings:

- **Dry and hydrated products cannot be compared directly.** Dry products (n = 9) have a median of 58.3 g per 100 g; hydrated foods (n = 43) 4.7 g [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. Rehydrating dried TVP at about 1 part TVP to 2 parts water gives roughly 21 g protein per 100 g at about VND 10,900 per 100 g (our calculation: 64 g and VND 32,700 per 100 g dry, each divided by 3). That is close to An Nhien's frozen gluten fish fillet (19 g, VND 23,200 per 100 g) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Low}.
- **Tofu is not a fixed protein unit.** Co.op Select white tofu (300 g) shows 3.8 g per 100 g, against 8.9 to 9.3 g for firmer tofus [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. Water content is a formulation choice.
- **Seafood-style gel analogues** (crab stick, "seafood tofu") sit at about 3 g per 100 g [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Plant milks** carry 1.3 to 2.5 g protein per 100 ml for soy milks and 0.7 to 1.1 g for oat and nut milks. Vinamilk's *cao đạm* (high-protein) plant milk reaches 5 g per 100 ml with pea protein [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
- One brand-wide average quoted by the collector in the Nha Trang field log for Fami soy milk (1.9 g per 100 ml) conflicts with the carton labels read in Ho Chi Minh City (2.5 g) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. We use the carton value.

## S2.6 Formulation archetypes A0 to A15

Each SKU row carries one archetype code. Protein statistics use unique products; price per 100 g of protein uses all SKU rows with both values [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.

| Code | Archetype | SKU rows | Products | Protein g/100 g, median (range; n) | VND per 100 g protein, median (range; n) | Main protein input | Typical makers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A0 | not a protein product, or insufficient data | 24 | 19 | n/a | n/a | n/a | instant noodles, unbranded rows |
| A1 | starch-and-vegetable filled wrapper | 38 | 26 | 3.95 (1.53 to 5.7; 14) | 368,548 (155,556 to 1,727,642; 17) | mung bean; wheat or rice wrapper; minor TVP or tofu skin | CJ Cau Tre, VISSAN, Cholimex, Co.op Select, LC Foods |
| A2 | wheat-dough bun or wheat-wrapper dim sum | 11 | 7 | 5.74 (5.0 to 6.3; 5) | 262,500 (173,055 to 572,674; 3) | wheat flour; soy protein in bibigo mandu | Cholimex, Co.op Select, MANI, bibigo |
| A3 | hydrated TVP or gluten analogue | 10 | 10 | 19.0 (12.0 to 25.1; 5) | 111,585 (65,990 to 175,000; 4) | wheat gluten, soy protein | An Nhien, Au Lac |
| A4 | gel or emulsion seafood analogue | 4 | 3 | 3.0 (3.0 to 3.03; 2) | 288,449 (278,667 to 471,947; 3) | soy milk, gluten, starch | Thoai An |
| A5 | dry TVP or gluten slices and chunks | 8 | 8 | 64.0 (53.3 to 66.7; 5) | 64,584 (48,976 to 85,053; 4) | soy protein, soy flour, gluten | An Nhien, Xuan Hong |
| A6 | canned soy luncheon or stew | 9 | 7 | 6.79 (4.5 to 9.08; 2) | 321,103 (223,704 to 418,502; 2) | soy protein, SPI, soybean | VISSAN, Ong Cha Va / NOSAFOOD |
| A7 | soy beverage | 14 | 14 | 2.25 (1.3 to 2.5; 6) | 91,667 (91,660 to 877,778; 3) | whole soybean | Vinasoy, Vinamilk, Ichiban |
| A8 | pea-protein-fortified plant milk | 2 | 2 | 5.0 (5.0; 2) | 174,306 (161,111 to 187,500; 2) | pea protein | Vinamilk |
| A9 | cereal or nut beverage | 32 | 24 | 1.05 (0.7 to 1.1; 6) | 890,909 (725,000 to 1,444,444; 3) | oat, almond, walnut | Oatly, 137 Degrees, TH, Veyo |
| A10 | tofu | 8 | 8 | 4.98 (3.8 to 9.3; 5) | 66,265 (39,171 to 121,053; 5) | soybean | Co.op Select, Ichiban, Tafu, Pulmuone |
| A11 | cultured or set nut, coconut or pea-oat product | 14 | 10 | 2.93 (1.6 to 9.7; 5) | 572,862 (510,526 to 892,487; 8) | cashew, coconut, pea protein, oat | Vinamilk, Deep Blue Island, Kashew |
| A12 | imported premium SPC or SPI analogue | 2 | 2 | 15.5 (15 to 16; 2) | 581,976 (542,424 to 621,528; 2) | SPC, SPI | Unconventional (Italy) |
| A13 | legume patty or spread (chickpea) | 3 | 3 | 9.0 (9.0; 2) | 447,812 (370,370 to 525,253; 2) | chickpea | Maris, Tartine |
| A14 | protein powder | 4 | 4 | 47.0 (41.2 to 58.3; 4) | 359,537 (343,029 to 365,634; 4) | pea, rice, hemp | Orgain, other imports |
| A15 | rice-based ready meal | 3 | 2 | 4.2 (4.2; 1) | 383,333 (383,333; 1) | rice | SG Food, bibigo |

The archetypes with the most SKU rows (A1, A9, A7) are the lowest in protein. The cheapest protein per đồng (A5 dry TVP, A10 tofu, A7 soy milk, A3 gluten analogues) is all soy- or wheat-based, and therefore import-based [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. Small n in most archetypes means the medians describe this sample only.

## S2.7 Price per 100 g and per 100 g of protein

Shelf price per 100 g (or 100 ml) and per 100 g of protein by product type, VND [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}:

| Product type | n (price) | Median per 100 g (range) | n (price and protein) | Median per 100 g protein (range) | Median per 100 g protein, USD (our calculation) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tofu | 5 | 3,643 (3,300 to 4,758) | 5 | 66,265 (39,171 to 121,053) | 2.55 |
| dried TVP or soy chunks (dry weight) | 5 | 32,667 (32,667 to 50,000) | 4 | 64,584 (48,976 to 85,053) | 2.48 |
| plant milk (per 100 ml) | 23 | 9,375 (2,292 to 17,556) | 8 | 456,250 (91,660 to 1,444,444) | 17.55 |
| plant yoghurt or creamer | 7 | 10,050 (9,700 to 15,311) | 6 | 534,210 (510,526 to 628,125) | 20.55 |
| dumpling, spring roll or bun | 35 | 11,425 (5,580 to 70,833) | 18 | 368,798 (155,556 to 1,727,642) | 14.18 |
| ready meal | 6 | 13,540 (12,200 to 16,100) | 3 | 297,619 (290,476 to 383,333) | 11.45 |
| frozen meat or seafood analogue | 18 | 15,180 (8,360 to 99,444) | 9 | 278,667 (65,990 to 621,528) | 10.72 |
| canned analogue | 7 | 30,811 (10,067 to 38,000) | 2 | 321,103 (223,704 to 418,502) | 12.35 |
| other | 4 | 40,303 (33,094 to 90,600) | 2 | 447,812 (370,370 to 525,253) | 17.22 |
| vegan cheese or spread | 9 | 83,333 (42,760 to 172,345) | 2 | 875,797 (859,107 to 892,487) | 33.68 |
| snack or jerky | 5 | 131,600 (131,600) | 0 | n/a | n/a |
| protein powder | 4 | 168,950 (150,641 to 199,986) | 4 | 359,537 (343,029 to 365,634) | 13.83 |

USD column: VND median divided by 26,000 (our calculation).

Readings:

- **Protein is cheapest in tofu and dried TVP**, at about VND 65,000 per 100 g of protein, and dearest in nut milks, yoghurts and cashew cheese [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Hydrated gluten or TVP analogues** (archetype A3) cost a median VND 111,585 per 100 g of protein, about one-fifth of the imported Italian SPC or SPI analogue (A12, VND 542,424 to 621,528) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Dried TVP prices are sensitive to the price source.** The field log used an online reference price of VND 49,000 per 150 g for An Nhien dried slices. AEON eShop listed VND 60,000 to 65,000 per 150 g on 23 September 2026 [@FORM-01; @FORM-19] {VN-direct|Medium}. With the AEON prices, price per 100 g of protein is 22 to 33% higher; dried TVP remains the cheapest non-tofu protein [@FORM-19] {VN-direct|Medium}. Both are logged in [[app-r2-disagreements]].
- **The same product varies in price between stores.** bibigo Healthy Mandu Chay (300 g) ranged from VND 43,000 (promotion) to 56,700, and VISSAN *chả giò chay* (spring roll) from VND 44,900 to 60,000 [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. Some of the spread is real, some is low-confidence reads. Single-store prices are not market prices.

| Unbranded *chả lụa chay*, 500 g | 10,580 | VISSAN *giò lụa* (pork roll), 500 g | 21,980 | -52% | Low (brand illegible) |

Only the VISSAN pair is a high-confidence, same-brand comparison: the chay spring roll is 38% cheaper per 100 g than the meat version [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. Because most chay wrappers hold about 2 to 6 g of protein per 100 g (median 4.3 g) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}, a cheaper pack is not cheaper protein. For supply-side purposes this matters: chay sells at or below the price of meat, so formulators have little room to pay more for protein ingredients.

Share of SKU rows by import flag, where the flag is known [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}:

| Group | n with a known flag | Y (imported) | Partial | N (domestic) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| All SKU rows | 170 | 77% | 11% | 12% |
| Locally made SKU rows | 131 | 70% | 14% | 16% |

Protein content by flag, unique locally made foods: N median 3.0 g per 100 g (maximum 4.6 g, n = 8); partial median 5.0 g (n = 6); Y median 7.6 g (range 1.6 to 66.7 g, n = 30) [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. Domestic protein ingredients today appear only in low-protein products.

Why soybeans count as imported:

> **Correction.** The wave 1 formulation note used USDA Post estimates for marketing year 2024/25: about 42,000 t of domestic soybeans against about 2.5 Mt of imports, a domestic share of about 1.6% [@FORM-09] {VN-direct|High}. The report now uses calendar-year 2025 customs data: Vietnam imported 2.61 Mt of soybeans in 2025 (USD 1.21 billion), which is about 98.4% of imports plus domestic output (domestic output 42 to 43 kt) [@MAC-09; @MAC-04] {VN-direct|Medium}. Origins in 2025: Brazil 1.20 Mt (45.8%), United States 1.14 Mt (43.6%), Canada 0.19 Mt (7.3%) [@MAC-09] {VN-direct|High}. The conclusion does not change: soy protein in Vietnamese food is almost entirely imported.

Why "domestic" mung bean is only partly domestic: Vietnam imported USD 138.3 million of mung and black gram beans (HS 0713.31) in 2023, mainly from Myanmar (65% of value), Cambodia (13%) and Argentina (8%) [@FORM-08] {VN-direct|Medium}. The reported tonnage (103,835 t) is imputed at a uniform unit value, so it is not a measurement [@FORM-08] {VN-direct|Medium}. Domestic mung bean production was not established. The import flag treats mung bean as domestic, so the shares above understate import dependence.

### Trade in concentrated plant-protein ingredients

China reports its exports to Vietnam by tonnage. Vietnam's own reported tonnages for these codes are imputed (every partner has the same unit value), so we use the China-reported tonnage and quote Vietnam-reported values [@FORM-02; @FORM-05] {VN-direct|High}.

TVP and SPC (2106.10) | 2023 | 7,957 t, USD 12.63 million | USD 1.59/kg | USD 33.98 million | United States 46%, China 27%, "Other Asia, nes" (usually read as Taiwan) 16%, India 5%, Netherlands 2%, Malaysia 2% | [@FORM-05; @FORM-02] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Same (2106.10) | 2024 | 10,029 t, USD 13.16 million | USD 1.31/kg | not yet reported | n/a | [@RGN-49] {VN-direct\|Medium} |

Cautions:

- **These codes are not an alt-protein market size.** HS 2106.10 and 3504 also carry meat-processing binders, dairy and supplement protein blends and peptones. The US share of HS 2106.10 is probably dairy or supplement blends rather than TVP (not verified) [@FORM-02] {VN-direct|Medium}. SPI is used as much by meat processors (*giò chả*, sausages) as by chay makers [@FORM-39] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **The China HS 3504 unit value (USD 1.63/kg in 2023, USD 1.03/kg in 2024) is far below SPI prices**, so much of that flow is probably lower-value or feed-grade protein substances [@RGN-48; @RGN-47] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Vietnam-reported and China-reported values differ.** For HS 2106.10 from China in 2023, Vietnam reported USD 9.15 million and 1,551 t; China reported USD 12.63 million and 7,957 t [@FORM-02; @FORM-05] {VN-direct|High}. We use China's tonnage (logged in [[app-r2-disagreements]]).

### Textured soy protein and soy protein concentrate

- **No Vietnamese TVP extruder was identified** in wave 1 or wave 2 [@FORM-01; @VCO-26] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- LC Foods specifies "soya TVP granule 4-7 mm" in a chay spring roll, a standard imported extrudate size; origin not stated [@FORM-28] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- An An Nhien chicken-ball label names soy protein from Serbia (logged as SPC); a retailer listing gives a different recipe (soy protein, corn starch, wheat fibre, soybean oil). We prefer the photographed label [@FORM-01; @FORM-18] {VN-direct|Medium}. The Serbian supplier is believed to be Sojaprotein (Becej), not verified.
- Thanh Dung, a chay maker in Ho Chi Minh City (former Binh Duong) founded in 2009, lists TVP among its products and says its raw materials are imported from the USA, Australia and Canada. Whether it extrudes or repacks is unknown [@FORM-35] {VN-direct|Low}.
- A Ho Chi Minh City machinery dealer, Tan Sao Bac A, sells Chinese soy-snack extrusion lines of 100 to 2,000 kg/h and 22 to 120 kW for dried chay "beef, chicken, fish, squid" [@FORM-34] {VN-direct|Medium}. This shows machines are on offer, not that TVP is made here.

### Soy protein isolate

- VMC Group (Phu Gia Viet My; Hanoi office; claims 19 branches) sells China-origin SPI in 20 kg bags for *giò chả*, sausages and vegetarian meat, and names Ingreda Vietnam and Luan Kha as other soy-protein distributors [@FORM-11; @FORM-39] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- We found no SPI, SPC, pea or rice protein isolate plant in Vietnam [@FORM-01; @VCO-16] {VN-direct|Medium}.

### Wheat gluten

- TDGIMEX (Hanoi) sells Chinese vital wheat gluten in 25 kg bags "for *mì căn* and vegetarian food"; VMC Group's Da Nang branch sells Xinrui (China) gluten in 25 kg bags [@FORM-12; @FORM-13] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Traditional *mì căn* can be washed out of wheat dough at small scale, but Vietnam grows no wheat, so both routes rest on imported wheat [@FORM-12; @MAC-01; @FORM-03] {VN-direct|Medium}. No Vietnamese wheat wet-milling (starch and gluten) plant was found. Uni-President Vietnam also mills wheat flour; whether it separates gluten was not checked [@VCO-29] {VN-direct|Low}.

### Tofu skin

- *Tàu hũ ky* is made in craft villages from mainly imported soybeans. Example: My Hoa village, Vinh Long (former Binh Minh town, former Vinh Long province): 27 households, over 200 workers, about 7 t per day (unclear whether product or beans). Producers prefer imported beans, saying they raise quality by over 20% [@FORM-14] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Imports of tofu skin from China are likely but were not measured.

### Soybeans and crushing

- Soybeans for tofu, soy milk and tofu skin are imported (see the correction in S2.9). USDA Post estimated food use at 540,000 t (MY2024/25) rising to 550,000 t [@FORM-09] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Domestic crushing is feed-grade.** VAL (Bunge-Wilmar joint venture) at Phu My 1 Industrial Park, Ho Chi Minh City (former Ba Ria-Vung Tau), can crush 2.6 Mt of soybeans and make nearly 2 Mt of meal a year after a USD 100 million second line (December 2025), and is expected by a Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee official to supply about 30% of the domestic soybean meal market for feed [@VCO-16; @FORM-10] {VN-direct|Medium}. It has no food-grade defatted flake or soy protein line on record [@VCO-16] {VN-direct|Medium}. A food-grade stream from such a crusher is the obvious domestic feedstock for Vietnamese TVP.

> **Correction.** The formulation note quoted soybean meal imports of "about 5.9 to 6 Mt a year" from the VAL press article [@FORM-10] {VN-direct|Medium}. The report uses 5.70 Mt of soybean meal imported in 2025 and 7.2 Mt fed [@MAC-04] {VN-direct|Medium}; see [[app-s6-feed-market]].

- **Domestic-bean tofu exists but is small.** ToFu House (Van Giang, Hung Yen; founded 2021) reported 150 to 500 t per month of tofu capacity and pilot soybean fields in Hai Phong, Lang Son and former Bac Kan (now Thai Nguyen) in 2023 [@FORM-36] {VN-direct|Medium}.

### Pea protein, chickpea, oats and nuts

All are imported or rest on imported raw material. No Vietnamese pea protein producer was found; Vinamilk's pea protein origin is not disclosed [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Low}. Cashew is processed in Vietnam, largely from imported raw nuts; this is counted as partial import dependence [@FORM-01; @EXP-18] {VN-direct|Low}.

### A fragmented buyer base

A 2022 to 2023 survey covered 126 vegetarian food production, processing and trading establishments in Hanoi alone (422 workers interviewed; 24.5% had acceptable food safety knowledge) [@FORM-37] {VN-direct|Medium}. There are many small buyers of TVP and gluten beyond the branded makers seen on shelves.

### Ingredient cost as a share of retail price

- **Dried TVP retails at 8 to 12 times the import unit value.** Retail dried TVP costs VND 327,000 to 500,000 per kg [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}; the 2023 China-reported unit value of HS 2106.10 exports to Vietnam was USD 1.59/kg, about VND 41,300 per kg at VND 26,000 per USD (our calculation: 327,000 / 41,340 = 7.9; 500,000 / 41,340 = 12.1) [@FORM-05] {VN-direct|Low}.
- **Gluten is roughly 5 to 7% of the retail price of a 19 g protein gluten analogue** (our calculation). Inputs: analogue at VND 23,200 per 100 g (VND 232,000 per kg) and 19 g protein per 100 g [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|Medium}; vital wheat gluten assumed at about 75% protein and supplying all the protein, so about 253 g of gluten per kg of product; gluten at USD 1.73/kg (China-reported) to USD 2.52/kg (Vietnam-reported, all origins) [@FORM-07; @FORM-03] {VN-direct|High}, converted at VND 26,000 per USD. Result: VND 11,400 to 16,600 of gluten per kg, or 4.9 to 7.2% of the retail price {VN-direct|Low}. This is modelled arithmetic, not company cost data.

Implication: a domestic TVP needs an ex-works price near the China-reported unit value of exports to Vietnam (USD 1.59/kg, about VND 41,300 per kg at VND 26,000 per USD, our calculation; before freight, duty and distributor margin) to compete head-on [@FORM-05] {VN-direct|Medium}. Formulators may pay a modest premium for consistency, non-GMO status, traceability or local supply security, but not a large one, because chay sells at or below meat prices (section S2.8).

## S2.11 Technology level

- **Extrusion.** 26 SKU rows contain an extruded soy ingredient (TVP or SPC, stated or inferred), from An Nhien, bibigo, VISSAN, Cau Tre, Cholimex, LC Foods, SG Food, Xuan Hong and Unconventional [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. The extrusion itself appears to happen abroad (section S2.10).
- **High-moisture extrusion (whole-muscle texture).** None seen, apart from what the imported Italian burger and sausage (Unconventional; SPC, SPI and rehydrated textured soy) may use [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Fermentation.** 15 SKU rows involve fermentation, all conventional: Vinamilk plant yoghurts (*S. thermophilus*, *L. bulgaricus*), cultured cashew cheeses (Kashew, Deep Blue Island) and imported nutritional yeast [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}. No biomass fermentation, mycoprotein or koji-based product was seen.
- **Precision-fermented or cultivated ingredients.** None on any label [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Mushroom as a meat base.** One local product (An Nhien *thịt ủ chân nấm chay*, VND 136,000 per 500 g) and imported mushroom jerky. Mushrooms appear in 42 rows, but for texture and flavour [@FORM-01] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Protein upgrading.** CJ Foods Vietnam's current *há cảo chay* (dumpling) and *chả giò bánh rế chay đặc biệt* labels contain no soy protein or tofu skin: mung bean is the only protein ingredient [@FORM-22; @FORM-23] {VN-direct|High}. An older Nha Trang listing of the 600 g spring roll included tofu skin, which suggests a reformulation away from soy (logged in [[app-r2-disagreements]]).
