**What the draft does, as described in Government press** [@REG2-05; @REG2-06] {VN-direct|Medium}:

- Four policy groups: reform of the management approach, stronger post-market control, digital transformation, and street food and catering.
- Two product groups. Group one: foods that must register a declaration or declare the applied standard (*công bố tiêu chuẩn áp dụng*) before circulation. Group two: foods that need no declaration. Both are inspected "throughout circulation on the market".
- The registration group named in the press is medical nutrition foods, foods for special diets, nutrition products for children up to 36 months, and health supplements.
- The drafters rejected requiring all pre-packaged processed foods to register a conformity declaration (the Decree 46/2026 approach) as "not suited to the management method".
- Advertising of medical nutrition foods and of products for children up to 36 months would be banned.

**What it lacks.** None of the draft summaries, the MOH submission or the stakeholder comments we read mentions *thực phẩm mới* (new food), new ingredients, history of use or a sandbox [@REG-08; @REG-10; @REG-16; @REG2-05; @REG2-06] {VN-direct|Medium}. We did not read the draft text itself or the WTO attachment. We do not know whether the recall ground in Art 55(1)(c) is carried over.

**Timing.** A trade source gave submission to the National Assembly in October 2026 and entry into force on 1 January 2027 [@REG2-04; @REG-12] {VN-direct|Medium}. The National Assembly Standing Committee settled the question on 24 September 2026: the law passes in two readings, with first comments at the October 2026 session and consideration for passage at the May 2027 session [@APR-07] {VN-direct|Medium}. So the 1 January 2027 start date cannot hold, and the window to add a new-food clause runs from the October 2026 session into early 2027, while the draft is revised between readings (our reading) [@REG-12; @APR-07] {VN-direct|Medium}. Our own search of the legal database on 23 September 2026 found no enacted law.

{{kn:kn-food-law-window}}

**What it means for new proteins.** Ordinary plant-based and fermented protein foods would fall in either the "declare the applied standard" group or the "no declaration" group. Neither involves pre-approval. So the new law, as described, keeps an open door but also keeps the uncertainty: there is still no way to get a new ingredient positively cleared. This is our reading [@REG2-05; @REG2-06] {VN-direct|Medium}.

> **Correction.** Wave 1 described the product-declaration design as three risk tiers, based on the July 2025 MOH submission. In fact that submission proposes two mechanisms and only cites the three risk tiers of the amended 2025 Law on Product and Goods Quality [@REG-16] {VN-direct|Medium}. The July 2026 Government press describes two groups [@REG2-05; @REG2-06] {VN-direct|Medium}. We use the later description; the Quality Law tiers may still shape the "declare" group {VN-direct|Medium}. See DG-113.

## S9.4 GMO rules and precision fermentation (Decree 43/2026)

### S9.4.1 Instruments

The GMO rules sit in Decree 69/2010/ND-CP on biosafety, as amended by Decree 123/2018 and Decree 43/2026/ND-CP; Decree 43/2026 repealed Decrees 108/2011 and 118/2020 [@REG-18; @REG-24] {VN-direct|High}. Decree 43/2026 was issued on 26 January 2026 and took effect the same day. It amends Decree 65/2010 (Biodiversity Law), Decree 69/2010, Decree 59/2017 (genetic resources, Chapter III) and Decree 66/2019 (wetlands) [@REG-18; @REG-24] {VN-direct|High}.

> **Correction.** In v0.6 this said Decree 43/2026 does not amend Decree 59/2017 on genetic resources; the source says it does (Chapter III), and it also amends Decree 66/2019.

### S9.4.2 Definitions

- **Gene-edited organisms** (*sinh vật chỉnh sửa gen*) are now in scope. The Biodiversity Law, as amended by Law 146/2025/QH15, defines them as containing no new genetic material. Owners self-determine their status, report to MAE and keep records for 10 years [@REG-18; @REG-43] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Product of a GMO:** "*sản phẩm được tạo ra từ sinh vật biến đổi gen có chứa vật liệu di truyền hoặc protein từ gen biến đổi*" (a product created from a GMO that contains GM genetic material or protein from the modified gene) [@REG-18; @REG2-11] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Refined products.** USDA and ISAAA report that highly refined products such as soybean oil and corn starch are excluded from "GM food" [@REG-19; @REG-20] {VN-adjacent|Medium}. The text extract did not show an explicit exclusion, but the definition already excludes anything with no GM DNA and no GM protein. A precision-fermented protein is not excluded, because it is itself protein from the modified gene [@REG-18] {VN-direct|Medium}. See DG-050.

### S9.4.3 Certificate for food and feed use (merged procedure)

Decree 43/2026 merges the old Art 32 to 33 into one MAE procedure that certifies a GMO as eligible for use as food and feed [@REG-18; @REG-21] {VN-direct|High}.

- **Criteria.** A biosafety council finds no uncontrollable risk, or at least 5 developed OECD or G20 countries allow the event [@REG-18; @REG-23] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Steps.** 5 WD to accept the dossier and form the council; 67 WD for a full council review, or 17 WD on the 5-country route; for a food-use certificate, MOH is consulted after the council (3 WD to send, 7 WD to reply); then 5 WD to decide. Public comment runs 20 WD (10 WD on the 5-country route) alongside the council review [@REG-23; @REG-22; @REG-24] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Food implies feed.** A GMO approved as food qualifies as feed [@REG-22] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Who runs it.** MAE's procedure list places this procedure with the MAE Department of Science and Technology [@REG2-12] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **End-to-end time.** Agency steps add up to 37 WD (5-country route) or 87 WD (full review) for food use, and 32 or 82 WD for feed only, where the decision takes 10 WD and MOH is not consulted (our calculation). USDA gives 45 and 90 WD. We use about 45 or 90 WD end to end [@REG-19; @REG-23; @REG-24] {VN-direct|Medium}. See DG-049.

### S9.4.4 Closed-production certificate (new Art 37a)

Decree 43/2026 adds Art 37a to Decree 69/2010: "*Giấy chứng nhận sinh vật biến đổi gen đủ điều kiện sử dụng trong sản xuất khép kín*" (certificate that a GMO is eligible for use in closed production) [@REG-18] {VN-direct|High}. This is the certificate a precision-fermentation plant using a GM production strain in Vietnam would need.

| Item | What the text says | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Strain conditions (Art 37a(2) and (3)) | The GMO comes from safe donor and recipient organisms and has a safety history in closed production under OECD or G20 standards | [@REG2-11] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Facility conditions | A closed system that prevents release into the environment; waste and emission treatment licensed by the environmental authority; operation to OECD or G20 closed-production standards | [@REG2-11] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Dossier (Art 37a(4)) | Application form (*Mẫu* 32) and technical description (*Mẫu* 33) | [@REG2-11] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Filing | In person, by post or online, with MAE. Completeness check at once for in-person filing and within 1 WD otherwise. Incomplete dossiers are refused in writing | [@REG2-11] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Issuer | MAE issues, re-issues and revokes certificates | [@REG2-11] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Timeline, council, validity, fee | Art 37a(4)(b): the MAE Minister forms a biosafety council within 5 WD, the council reviews within 50 WD, and the Minister decides within 5 WD (about 60 WD; time to supplement the dossier is not counted). Validity and fee were not visible | [@REG-24; @REG2-11; @REG2-12] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| Issuing level | Both the decree (the MAE Minister decides) and Decision 375/QĐ-BNNMT (29 January 2026) place the procedure at central level, with the MAE Department of Nature Conservation and Biodiversity (*Cục Bảo tồn thiên nhiên và Đa dạng sinh học*) | [@REG2-11; @REG2-12] {VN-direct\|Medium} |

DG-111 recorded an issuing-level conflict; there is none, as both texts place the procedure at central level.

### S9.4.5 What this means for precision-fermented proteins

- A purified recombinant protein contains "protein from the modified gene", so it is probably a "product of a GMO" [@REG-18; @REG2-11] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- GM labelling then applies when it is more than 5% of total ingredients (Decree 15/2018 Art 10; Joint Circular 45/2015 Art 1(1)), but not to GM food in which neither the modified gene nor its product can be detected (Art 1(2)(a)) [@REG-02; @LBL-10] {VN-direct|High}. Lactoferrin in a Vietnamese formula is used at about 0.08% (80 mg per 100 g), about 60 times below the trigger (our calculation) [@LBL-25] {VN-direct|Medium}. So the label bites on high-inclusion uses, such as a drink whose main protein is precision-fermented; whether an identical recombinant protein counts as a "detectable product of the modified gene" is not settled by any text or letter.
- Making it in Vietnam with a GM microbe needs the Art 37a closed-production certificate [@REG-18; @REG2-11] {VN-direct|High}.
- No article covers products made with GMOs that contain no viable GMO. The food-use certificate is written for organisms, not products. So no text says whether a purified protein also needs a food-use certificate. Imported precision-fermented ingredients face the same labelling question [@REG2-11] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Food-use certification of GMOs now sits fully with MAE, with MOH consulted [@REG-21; @REG-22] {VN-direct|Medium}.

> **Correction.** Earlier drafts did not treat precision-fermented proteins as GMO products. Under Decree 43/2026 they probably are, because the definition includes "protein from the modified gene" [@REG-18; @REG2-11] {VN-direct|Medium}. This is the single most important open legal question for precision fermentation in Vietnam. A joint written question to MAE and VFA is the cheapest way to close it.

## S9.5 Food additives, enzymes and processing aids

- **Circular 24/2019/TT-BYT** (30 August 2019, effective 16 October 2019) sets the permitted additive list. Art 4 bases the list on Codex (CAC) and JECFA [@REG-25] {VN-direct|High}.
- New uses, or mixed additives with new functions, must be registered at VFA (Art 11(2)) [@REG-25] {VN-direct|High}. Registration takes 7 WD under Decree 15/2018 Art 8 (scope in Art 6) [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- Organisations may propose additions to the list with scientific safety evidence (Art 17(3)(d)) [@REG-25] {VN-direct|High}.
- The extract did not show a separate pathway for enzymes or processing aids, or anything on GM-derived additives. Amendments after 2019 were not visible [@REG-25] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Route for a new additive or enzyme: registration of the product declaration at VFA, or a request to MOH to amend the list [@REG-02; @REG-25] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S9.6 Health supplements

- Health supplements need MOH registration within 21 WD and a GMP-certified plant (Decree 15/2018 Art 8, 11 and 12) [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- This is a real route for microalgae (spirulina, chlorella) and concentrated protein ingredients sold as supplements [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- The draft Food Safety Law keeps a GMP requirement for health-supplement manufacturers [@REG2-05] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S9.7 Labelling, claims and fortification

- **The goods-label decree.** Decree 37/2026/ND-CP (23 January 2026) replaced Decree 43/2017/ND-CP and its amendment Decree 111/2021/ND-CP [@LBL-07; @LBL-08] {VN-direct|Medium}. Food labels still carry the name, ingredients or quantified ingredients, nutrition, *thông tin cảnh báo* (warning information), dates, storage and instructions for use [@REG-26; @LBL-09] {VN-direct|Medium}. We could not read the new label chapter (the text stopped at Art 32), so its article numbers are unknown; exact-phrase searches show that its text keeps the name, quantity and GM wording of the old decree [@LBL-09] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **The misleading-name and quantity rules, now verified.** Decree 43/2017 Art 11: "*Tên hàng hóa không được làm hiểu sai lệch về bản chất, công dụng và thành phần của hàng hóa*" (the name must not mislead about the nature, use or composition of the goods). Art 13(4): an ingredient whose name is used as, or as part of, the product name "*bắt buộc phải ghi định lượng*" (must be quantified), a rule carried into Decree 37/2026 [@LBL-06; @LBL-07; @LBL-08; @LBL-09] {VN-direct|Medium}. By our count from Vissanmart product pages, Vissan already prints the named meat's share on 28 of 29 meat-named formulations [@BUY-05] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **No allergen list.** The warning information in Appendix I item 2 of Decree 111/2021 had no defined content and no allergen list. Circular 05/2019/TT-BKHCN Art 9 covers technical specifications and warnings, also with no allergen list [@REG2-24; @REG2-25] {VN-direct|Medium}. So Vietnam has no mandatory allergen declaration list of the Codex type. Whether Circular 05/2019, which guided Decree 43/2017, still applies was not checked.
- **No reserved names.** We found no rule that reserves *thịt* (meat), *sữa* (milk) or *phô mai* (cheese), and none that governs *chay* (vegetarian) or *thuần chay* (vegan) as names (our search of legal texts and standards, 25 September 2026). Decree 111/2021 had no such rule [@REG2-24] {VN-direct|Medium}; we did not read the label chapter of Decree 37/2026, which replaced it. TCVN 11216:2015 defines milk without a Codex-style clause restricting dairy terms, and QCVN 28:2026/BCT (Circular 09/2026/TT-BCT, in force 1 September 2026) covers liquid dairy products only, including skimmed milk blended with vegetable fat [@FTR-07; @LBL-16; @LBL-17] {VN-direct|Medium}. TCVN 12443:2018 is itself titled *Sữa đậu nành* (soy milk) and needs at least 2.0 g of protein per 100 ml for the name [@FTR-06] {VN-direct|Medium}. Makers qualify meat words, as in Vissan's *Heo hầm chay* (chay stewed pork) and *Ragu bò chay* [@BUY-05] {VN-direct|High}. The only state use of a new-meat name we found is *thịt nhân tạo* (artificial meat) for stem-cell meat in a 2025 Bac Ninh biotechnology scheme [@LBL-20] {VN-direct|Low}.
- **Meat content.** TCVN 7049:2020 (heat-treated processed meat), TCVN 7050:2020 (not heat treated) and TCVN 7048:2020 (canned meat) set no minimum meat or protein content and do not mention plant protein [@LBL-11; @LBL-12; @LBL-13] {VN-direct|Medium}. A meat product with a plant or fungal extender keeps its name; if the name names the meat, the meat share must be printed.
- **Vegetarian and vegan claims.** TCVN 13625:2023 (ISO 23662:2021, voluntary) defines them. "Vegetarian" allows egg, milk and honey; "vegan" excludes every animal-derived input, including processing aids; the standard says nothing on alliums, so it is broader than Buddhist *chay* [@LBL-15] {VN-direct|High}. A false chay claim is already unlawful under the goods-label rules [@LBL-06] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **GM labelling:** above 5% of total ingredients, and not where neither the modified gene nor its product can be detected (Decree 15/2018 Art 10; Joint Circular 45/2015/TTLT-BNNPTNT-BKHCN Art 1) [@REG-02; @LBL-10] {VN-direct|High}. See S9.4.5.
- **Nutrition labelling.** Circular 29/2023/TT-BYT made energy, protein, carbohydrate, fat and sodium mandatory on non-exempt pre-packaged foods from 1 January 2026. Circular 30/2026/TT-BYT replaced it on 10 July 2026 with the same core rules: the protein reference value is 50 g, showing the percentage is optional, and foods made by small food businesses are exempt [@LBL-01; @LBL-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Claims.** TCVN 14429:2025 (voluntary, from Codex CAC/GL 23) sets "source of protein" at 10% of the reference value per 100 g, 5% per 100 kcal or 10% per serving, and "high" (*cao*) at twice that: 5 g and 10 g per 100 g, or 2.5 g and 5 g per 100 kcal (our calculation with the 50 g reference value in TCVN 7088:2025) [@LBL-03; @LBL-04] {VN-direct|High}. Claims for added micronutrients need 10% of the reference intake (Circular 43/2014 Art 8) [@LBL-05] {VN-direct|High}. A content claim needs no registration and no advertising approval; the 2025 Advertising Law amendment (Law 75/2025) and Decree 342/2025 add truthfulness and endorser duties, not approvals [@REG-02; @LBL-18; @LBL-19] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Fortification.** Decree 09/2016/ND-CP (in force) makes iodine, iron, zinc and vitamin A the mandatory fortificants: salt for eating and processing must be iodised, wheat flour used in food processing must carry iron and zinc, and soy, palm, rapeseed and peanut oil must carry vitamin A, except oil for industrial processing [@NQR-02] {VN-direct|Medium}. No protein food is a vehicle, so tofu, textured soy and soy milk carry nothing by rule. A 2025 amendment draft concerned iodised salt in fish sauce, and we found no amending decree [@NQR-03] {VN-direct|Low}. A voluntarily fortified food self-declares under Decree 15/2018 unless it is a health supplement, a medical food, a special-diet food or a nutrition product for children up to 36 months, which must register [@NQR-04] {VN-direct|High}.

The instruments are in `instruments.csv` (INS-067 to INS-078) and `label_rules.csv`.

> **Correction.** Wave 1 believed that the warning requirement covered allergens through guidance under Circular 05/2019/TT-BKHCN, but could not verify it. Wave 2 read Decree 111/2021 and Circular 05/2019 and found no allergen list in either [@REG2-24; @REG2-25] {VN-direct|Medium}. Voluntary allergen labelling is prudent for soy, wheat-gluten and insect-based foods because the law is silent.

> **Correction.** Earlier drafts cited Decree 43/2017 as amended by Decree 111/2021 as the label decree in force and Circular 29/2023 as the nutrition-label circular. Decree 37/2026 replaced the first on 23 January 2026 and Circular 30/2026 the second on 10 July 2026 [@LBL-08; @LBL-02] {VN-direct|Medium}. The rules that matter for new proteins carry over.

## S9.8 Halal

- Decision 10/QĐ-TTg (2023) approves the scheme to strengthen international cooperation for Vietnam's halal industry to 2030. It was listed, not read [@REG-28] {VN-direct|Low}.
- Decree 127/2026/ND-CP (6 April 2026, effective 1 June 2026) is the first decree on halal quality management and development [@REG-27] {VN-direct|High}:
  - Certification is voluntary unless another law requires it.
  - Certifiers register with MOST (Art 13) and need at least 2 Muslim expert assessors (Art 11).
  - Standards may be national (for example TCVN 13888:2023), international or those of a partner country.
  - The state budget can support testing and certification costs for export-oriented firms (Art 23). Art 16 covers mutual recognition.
  - The decree says nothing about GM, fermentation-derived or cell-based ingredients.
- Relevance: halal certification of fermentation-derived proteins (media, strains) will follow each certifier's standard [@REG-27] {VN-direct|Medium}. Malaysia ruled in December 2025 that cultivated meat can be halal under conditions, the first Muslim-majority country to do so [@RGN-20] {VN-adjacent|Medium}. We did not verify recognition of Vietnamese certificates by JAKIM (Malaysia) or BPJPH (Indonesia).

## S9.9 Imports of food and feed ingredients

- **Food.** Under Decree 15/2018, imported food is subject to state inspection, with exemptions (Art 13) for products that already hold a registered product declaration, personal and diplomatic imports, goods for export processing, and raw materials for internal production [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- The suspended Decree 46/2026 would have tightened import inspection [@REG-03; @REG-08] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- MOIT issued Circular 28/2026/TT-BCT on the list of imported goods under food safety inspection. It was listed, not read [@REG-17] {VN-direct|Low}.
- **Livestock feed.** Provinces issue import licences for feed not yet published, within 10 WD, and run state quality inspection of imported feed [@REG-35] {VN-direct|High}. Law on Animal Husbandry Art 37 requires a trial for certain first imports from countries whose trial procedures Vietnam does not recognise [@REG-29] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Aquafeed.** Import licences are needed only for unlisted products imported for trials, research or fairs (Law on Fisheries Art 36) [@REG-37] {VN-direct|High}. Provincial chairs issue them (Decree 136/2025 Art 18(2)) [@REG-41] {VN-direct|High}. Circular 16/2026 Art 18(2)(c) lets firms import feed for research with an approved research outline [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}.
- **Testing.** FIRI's NACEFA laboratory holds ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation (VILAS 259) and is MAE-designated to test imported feed ingredients against QCVN 01-190:2020 [@INF-03] {VN-direct|High}.

## S9.10 Livestock feed

### S9.10.1 The legal chain

**Law on Animal Husbandry 32/2018/QH14** (19 November 2018; effective 1 January 2020), amended by Law 146/2025/QH15 from 1 January 2026 [@REG-29; @REG-43] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 32: before circulation, commercial feed needs a published standard and conformity declaration, a certified factory, product information on the MAE portal, and a label.
- Art 33: compound and concentrate feed are self-published.
- Art 34: supplement feed is appraised before publication.
- Art 36: MAE publishes traditional feeds and single raw materials by name and technical requirements. Feed for internal use and custom orders is exempt.
- Art 37: feed trials are required for (a) certain first imports from countries whose trial procedures Vietnam does not recognise, and (b) feed containing a *chất mới* (new substance) not yet trialled in Vietnam, except the recognised results of state research projects. Art 37(4) empowers the Minister to issue the permitted raw-material list.
- Law 146/2025 amended Art 37 wording on the Minister's list of banned chemicals, biological products and microorganisms. The "new substance" trial trigger was not visible in the amended text [@REG2-03] {VN-direct|Low}.

**Decree 13/2020/ND-CP** (21 January 2020), amended by Decree 46/2022 and Decree 32/2026 [@REG-30; @REG-31; @REG-35] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 9 to 11: factory conditions and certificates. Art 11 is the on-site assessment of factory conditions, with surveillance every 24 months (36 months with ISO, GMP or HACCP).
- Art 13: import of feed not yet published (licensing).
- Art 15: recognition of exporting countries' trial and recognition procedures.
- Art 17 to 18: state quality inspection.
- None of these articles concerns trials of new feed. Art 31 concerns trials of livestock waste-treatment products.

> **Correction.** A prior lead said that Decree 13/2020 Art 11 requires a feed trial lasting 12 to 18 months. Art 11 is about factory inspection. Feed trials come from Law on Animal Husbandry Art 37 and Circular 94/2025/TT-BNNMT Chapter III [@REG-29; @REG-30; @REG-34] {VN-direct|High}. No text gives "12 to 18 months". Documented agency time is about 40 WD plus the trial itself. Our estimate of the total is 6 to 18 months (see below). See DG-051 and DG-052.

### S9.10.2 The permitted raw-material list

**Circular 21/2019/TT-BNNPTNT** (28 November 2019), amended by **Circular 31/2022/TT-BNNPTNT** (30 December 2022, effective 20 February 2023) [@REG-32; @REG-33] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 6: the permitted list is Appendix VI. DLPAH "*tổng hợp, trình Bộ trưởng … cập nhật Danh mục … định kỳ hằng năm*" (compiles and submits to the Minister to update the list periodically every year).
- Appendix VI section I.1.2 (terrestrial animal origin) names "*bột xương, bột thịt, … côn trùng, động vật không xương sống …*" (bone meal, meat meal, … insects, invertebrates …).
- Section I.2 (plant origin) lists among coarse feeds the aquatic plants "*rong, rêu, tảo, bèo*" (seaweed, moss, algae, duckweed).
- Section II lists vitamins, minerals, amino acids, enzymes, probiotics (Bacillus, Lactobacillus, *Saccharomyces cerevisiae*) and technical additives.
- Circular 31/2022 added inactive yeasts to section I.6: irradiated, hydrolysed or dried Torula or Candida yeast, yeast cultured on molasses, dried yeast, and by-products of amino-acid production.

**Status in September 2026.** The list is still Circular 21/2019 Appendix VI as amended by Circular 31/2022. Circular 94/2025 Art 18 repeals Art 4, 5 and 6 of Circular 22/2019 (breeds), Art 1(2) of Circular 21/2024 and items of Circular 09/2025, none of which touches the list, and has no list of its own [@REG-33; @REG2-08; @REG2-09] {VN-direct|High}. We found no 2024 to 2026 amendment adding *protein đơn bào* (single-cell protein) or *sinh khối vi sinh vật* (microbial biomass) [@REG-33; @REG2-09] {VN-direct|Medium}. Search listings can miss documents, so DLPAH should confirm this.

**What this means.** Insects, duckweed, algae and inactive yeasts need no trial for livestock feed. They still need a certified factory, a conformity declaration against QCVN 01-190:2020 and a label [@REG-32; @REG-33; @REG-36] {VN-direct|High}. We found no explicit entry for bacterial single-cell protein (SCP), fungal mycoprotein or precision-fermented proteins [@REG-32; @REG2-09] {VN-direct|Medium}.

### S9.10.3 Feed trials (Circular 94/2025/TT-BNNMT)

Circular 94/2025/TT-BNNMT (31 December 2025, effective 1 January 2026), Chapter III (Art 13 to 14) [@REG-34] {VN-direct|High}:

- Trial content: quality, safety or toxicity, and effects on animals. Methods suit each feed type, and duration is set in the protocol.
- DLPAH receives the protocol, forms an appraisal council within 15 WD, and approves within 5 WD after revision.
- Results recognition takes 15 + 5 WD.
- "*Kết quả khảo nghiệm được công nhận là căn cứ để đưa vào danh mục nguyên liệu được phép sử dụng làm thức ăn chăn nuôi*" (a recognised trial result is the basis for adding the material to the permitted list).
- It replaced parts of Circular 22/2019, Circular 21/2024 and Circular 09/2025.

The trial must be run at a qualified trial facility (Law Art 37(3)) [@REG-29] {VN-direct|High}. MAE merged its livestock trial and veterinary drug testing centres into the Central Livestock and Veterinary Trial and Testing Centre I (Hanoi) by Decision 3064/QĐ-BNNMT of 4 August 2026, effective 1 October 2026. The centre runs feed trials and may sell services [@INF-18] {VN-direct|High}.

### S9.10.4 Safety limits (QCVN 01-190:2020/BNNPTNT)

QCVN 01-190:2020/BNNPTNT (Circular 04/2020, amended by Circulars 08/2020 and 05/2021) sets maximum limits for arsenic, cadmium, lead, mercury, aflatoxin B1, *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, HCN, gossypol and other hazards in feed and raw materials. Traditional single raw materials need a conformity declaration (*công bố hợp quy*) before sale, except household production and custom orders [@REG-36] {VN-direct|High}.

### S9.10.5 Provincial devolution (Decree 32/2026/ND-CP)

Decree 32/2026/ND-CP (effective 21 January 2026) moves several procedures to provinces [@REG-35] {VN-direct|High}:

- compound and concentrate feed: self-declared on the portal;
- supplement feed: appraised by the province within 15 WD;
- import licences for feed not yet published: province, 10 WD;
- import quality inspection: provincial chair.

Decree 136/2025 had already moved other agriculture and environment powers to provinces from 1 July 2025 [@REG-41] {VN-direct|High}.

### S9.10.6 Penalties (Decree 211/2026/ND-CP)

Decree 211/2026/ND-CP (16 June 2026, effective 5 August 2026) on administrative penalties in animal husbandry [@REG2-10] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 22(1): "*Phạt tiền từ 10.000.000 đồng đến 15.000.000 đồng đối với hành vi sử dụng mỗi loại nguyên liệu không có trong Danh mục nguyên liệu được phép sử dụng*" (a fine of VND 10 to 15 million for using each type of raw material not in the permitted list), when the goods are worth under VND 200 million or the illicit profit is under VND 100 million.
- Art 22(2): VND 15 to 20 million at higher values.
- Additional penalty: suspension of feed production for 1 to 3 months.
- Remedies: surrender of illicit profit and forced repurposing of the material, or destruction if that is impossible.

At 26,000 VND per USD, VND 10 to 20 million is about USD 385 to 770 per material (our calculation). The fine is small, but the production suspension is not. For a new SCP or fungal biomass, running the trial first (or waiting for a list update) is now clearly worth its cost.

### S9.10.7 Steps for a new single raw material (for example bacterial SCP or cassava-pulp fungal protein)

1. Check the permitted list (Circular 21/2019 Appendix VI as amended). If the material fits an existing entry (for example *nấm men*, yeast; *côn trùng*, insects; *bèo*, duckweed), no trial is needed [@REG-32; @REG-33] {VN-direct|High}.
2. If not, treat it as a "new substance". Run a trial under an approved protocol (Circular 94/2025 Chapter III) at a qualified facility. Importing trial samples may need a provincial import licence [@REG-34; @REG-35] {VN-direct|High}.
3. Get the result recognised by DLPAH, then wait for the annual list update or rely on the recognition decision [@REG-32; @REG-34] {VN-direct|High}. Whether recognition alone allows circulation before the list update is not stated in the texts read.
4. Get a certified factory (province), a declared standard, conformity with QCVN 01-190:2020, and a label [@REG-29; @REG-36; @REG-41] {VN-direct|High}.
5. If sold as supplement feed with a functional claim, get the province's appraisal (15 WD) [@REG-35] {VN-direct|High}.

**Documented agency time** is about 40 WD (protocol 15 + 5; results 15 + 5) [@REG-34] {VN-direct|High}. This excludes dossier preparation, the trial itself (likely one grow-out cycle per species) and the wait for the annual list update. **Our estimate of the total is 6 to 18 months.** It is an estimate, not a documented figure.

Law Art 37(2) exempts the recognised results of state research projects from separate trials [@REG-29] {VN-direct|High}. Publicly funded feed trials are therefore a high-leverage public good (policy option PO-021).

## S9.11 Aquafeed

### S9.11.1 The legal chain

**Law on Fisheries 18/2017/QH14** (21 November 2017), amended by Law 146/2025/QH15 (aquafeed changes not visible in the extract) [@REG-37; @REG2-03] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 31: before circulation, a published standard, a conformity declaration and information to MAE are needed. MAE issues the "*Danh mục hóa chất, chế phẩm sinh học, vi sinh vật, nguyên liệu sản xuất thức ăn được phép sử dụng*" (list of permitted chemicals, biological products, microorganisms and feed raw materials).
- Art 34: the Ministry issues factory certificates for foreign-invested firms. Whether that power moved to provinces was not verified.
- Art 35(1): aquafeed must be trialled "*trong trường hợp có hóa chất, chế phẩm sinh học, vi sinh vật, nguyên liệu sản xuất thức ăn thủy sản không có tên trong danh mục quy định*" (where it contains chemicals, biological products, microorganisms or aquafeed raw materials not on the prescribed list) [@REG2-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- Art 36: import licences are needed only for unlisted products imported for trials, research or fairs.

**Decree 26/2019/ND-CP** (8 March 2019), amended by Decree 37/2024 and Decree 309/2025 (the latter only on minimum catch sizes) [@REG-38; @REG-39] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 31: trial facility conditions.
- Art 32: the dossier (forms 17.NT registration, 18.NT protocol, 19.NT facility description). The authority appraises it within 20 days and issues a trial decision (form 21.NT). After the trial, results are recognised within 10 WD of the report.

**Decree 136/2025** (from 1 July 2025): Art 19(2) moves recognition of aquafeed trial results to the provincial People's Committee chair; Art 18(2) moves import licences for aquafeed with unlisted substances to the provincial chair [@REG-41] {VN-direct|High}.

Official aquafeed trials sit with one national centre with sub-centres in Can Tho (Region I) and Ho Chi Minh City (Region II), under Decision 1109/QĐ-BNNMT of 25 April 2025 [@INF-28; @INF-19] {VN-direct|High}.

### S9.11.2 Circular 16/2026/TT-BNNMT and its Appendix II

Circular 16/2026/TT-BNNMT (9 March 2026, effective the same day) replaces Circular 26/2018, Art 8 and Appendices XX to XXII of Circular 01/2022, and Art 3 to 6 of Circular 10/2025 [@REG-40] {VN-direct|High}. Art 12(2) says the permitted list is Appendix II. Art 19(1)(d) makes DFFI responsible for reviewing and updating it, with no stated way for firms to propose additions [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}.

**Structure of Appendix II** ("*Danh mục hoá chất, chế phẩm sinh học, vi sinh vật, nguyên liệu sản xuất thức ăn được phép sử dụng trong nuôi trồng thuỷ sản tại Việt Nam*") [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}:

- I. Chemicals: 1. minerals for aquafeed and environment products; 2. chemicals for environment treatment; 3. preservatives, antioxidants and other substances.
- II. Biological products, microorganisms, vitamins and amino acids: 1. bioactives and extracts from organisms (17 entries); 2. microorganisms (30 entries); 3. vitamins; 4. enzymes.
- **There is no raw-material section**, despite the title.

**Entries relevant to new proteins** [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}:

| Candidate | On the aquafeed list? | Entry (verbatim where available) |
|---|---|---|
| Insect meal (black soldier fly larvae) | No | none |
| Yeast protein, inactive yeast | Only as microorganisms | II.2 no. 8 "*Candida utilis*"; no. 22 "*Pichia farinosa*"; no. 27 "*Saccharomyces (Saccharomyces boulardii, Saccharomyces cerevisiae)*" |
| Yeast derivatives | Yes, as bioactives | II.1 no. 11 "β-Glucan" |
| Bacterial SCP (for example *Methylococcus*) | No | none |
| Microalgae (*Spirulina*, *Chlorella*, *Schizochytrium*) | No | none |
| Duckweed (*bèo*) | No | none |
| Fermented soybean meal | No (the fermenting microbes are listed) | II.2 no. 3 "*Aspergillus (Aspergillus niger, Aspergillus oryzae)*"; no. 4 *Bacillus* spp. including *B. subtilis*, *B. natto*, *B. licheniformis*, *B. amyloliquefaciens* |
| Chitin derivatives (insect or shrimp shell) | Yes, as bioactives | II.1 no. 4 "Chitosan-oligosaccharide"; no. 8 "Low-molecular-weight Chitosan" |

About 20 *Bacillus* species are listed. No methanotrophic bacteria and no microalgae are listed [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}.

> **Correction.** Wave 1 could not read the raw-material section of Appendix II and treated its content as unknown (our process note). Wave 2 read Appendix II three times and found that it has no raw-material section at all [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}.

### S9.11.3 Legal consequence: a trial trigger broader than practice

Read literally, Art 35(1) with a list that holds no raw materials catches every raw material, including fishmeal and soybean meal. Conventional feeds are evidently sold without trials, so practice differs from the text [@REG2-01; @REG2-02] {VN-direct|High}. The body of Circular 16/2026 does not say that livestock-list materials, or conventional materials, count as permitted in aquafeed [@REG2-01] {VN-direct|High}.

Our reading has two branches {VN-direct|Medium}:

- (a) the regulator treats conventional raw materials as outside the list requirement by practice, in which case insect meal and yeast protein probably are too; or
- (b) any unlisted raw material formally needs a trial.

The texts do not settle this. A written DFFI opinion is the cheapest fix. See DG-112. We found no penalty decree for aquafeed matching Decree 211/2026; this was not checked.

## S9.12 Tax and investment incentives

### S9.12.1 Corporate income tax

**Law on Corporate Income Tax 67/2025/QH15** (14 June 2025; effective 1 October 2025; applies from the 2025 tax period) [@REG-45] {VN-direct|Medium}:

- Art 12(2): incentives for (a) application of high technology under the High Technology Law and strategic technology; (e) high-tech enterprises, high-tech agriculture enterprises and science and technology enterprises; (i), (k), (l) agriculture and agricultural or aquatic processing meeting Art 4 conditions.
- Art 13(1): a 10% rate for 15 years for categories (a) to (e). Agricultural processing gets 10% or 15%, depending on location.
- Art 14(1): 4 years' exemption and a 50% cut for 9 years.
- Art 4: exempts some agricultural processing income in disadvantaged areas, and gives up to 3 years' exemption for products from newly applied technology.

**Decree 320/2025/ND-CP** (15 December 2025) guides the law and applies from the 2025 tax period [@REG2-18] {VN-direct|High}. Two tests matter for alternative protein:

- Art 4(1)(b): processed agricultural and aquatic products qualify for the exemption only if "*tỷ lệ giá trị nguyên vật liệu là nông sản, thủy sản trên chi phí sản xuất ... từ 30% trở lên*" (agricultural or aquatic raw materials are at least 30% of production cost), and the product is not subject to special consumption tax [@REG2-18] {VN-direct|High}. A cassava-based fermentation plant likely passes; a plant running on imported refined sugar may not. This is our interpretation {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Art 4(4)(b): "*Thu nhập từ bán sản phẩm làm ra từ công nghệ mới lần đầu tiên áp dụng ở Việt Nam được miễn thuế 03 năm*" (income from products made with technology applied for the first time in Vietnam is exempt for 3 years), subject to confirmation by the competent authority [@REG2-18] {VN-direct|High}. This could suit a first precision-fermentation or gas-fermentation plant.
- The incentive chapter (10% for 15 years; 4 years' exemption plus 9 years at 50% for new projects applying listed high technology) did not render, so the certification criteria remain unread [@REG2-18] {VN-direct|Medium}. MOF Decision 517/QĐ-BTC (20 March 2026) corrected Decree 320/2025 Art 20(1)(a), Art 23(10) and Art 24(2). We checked the decision on thuvienphapluat.vn; it is not yet in our source list {VN-direct|Medium}.

**VAT on feed.** Under the VAT Law 48/2024/QH15 (Art 5(3), in force 1 July 2025), animal feed and aquafeed are "not subject to VAT" [@COST-24] {VN-direct|High}. A plant making a feed protein therefore cannot reclaim VAT on its equipment, power and inputs; a food-ingredient plant can. Wave 1 estimated this adds roughly 5 to 10% to taxed input costs (our estimate; see [[app-s12-costs]]).

### S9.12.2 High-tech and strategic technology lists

**Decision 23/2026/QĐ-TTg** (15 May 2026, effective 1 July 2026) replaces Decision 38/2020 [@REG-47] {VN-direct|High}. Its priority high technologies include omics (item 48), synthetic and molecular biology (49), bioinformatics (50), new-generation microbial technology (51), tissue, embryo and cell technology in medicine and agriculture (52), and "technology for producing recombinant proteins, enzymes and monoclonal antibodies" (60). Its encouraged products include recombinant proteins and enzymes (92), advanced biological products (98), and microbial strains and products for health, agriculture and environment (100). Items 49, 60 and 92 fit precision fermentation; 51 and 100 fit biomass fermentation and SCP; 52 fits cultivated meat (our mapping). There is no item for food, feed or alternative protein as such [@REG-47] {VN-direct|High}.

**Decision 21/2026/QĐ-TTg** (30 April 2026, effective 1 July 2026) replaces Decision 1131/QĐ-TTg (2025). Strategic technology item 4 is "advanced biotechnology and biomedicine". Strategic products include new-generation biologics for livestock and aquaculture (item 14) and new-generation crop, livestock and aquatic varieties from cell technology and gene editing (item 16). There is no food or feed protein item [@REG-56] {VN-direct|High}.

The **Law on High Technology 133/2025/QH15** is cited as the basis for both decisions. We did not read it, and its effective date (1 July 2026) is inferred [@REG-47; @REG-56] {VN-direct|Low}. Decree 263/2026/NĐ-CP (effective 1 July 2026) lets provincial People's Committees set up hi-tech agriculture zones, with incentives that include priority for state R&D funds and up to 70% interest subsidy on loans to commercialise technology [@INF-23] {VN-direct|Medium}.

### S9.12.3 Investment Support Fund (Decree 182/2024/ND-CP)

Decree 182/2024/ND-CP (31 December 2024), Art 18 [@REG-46] {VN-direct|High}:

- High-tech product projects qualify with at least VND 12,000 bn of capital or VND 20,000 bn of annual revenue. Semiconductor and AI projects qualify at VND 6,000 bn or VND 10,000 bn.
- R&D centres need at least VND 3,000 bn, of which VND 1,000 bn within 3 years.
- Support: training up to 50%, R&D 20 to 30%, fixed assets 8 to 10%, high-tech products 1 to 3% of value added.
- Applications are due by 10 July of the following year.

At 26,000 VND per USD, the thresholds are about USD 460 million of capital or USD 770 million of revenue for a high-tech product project, and about USD 115 million for an R&D centre (our calculation). No alternative-protein project in Vietnam is near these sizes, so the fund is out of reach. See DG-053.

### S9.12.4 Law on Investment 2025

**Law on Investment 143/2025/QH15** (11 December 2025, effective 1 March 2026) [@REG-57] {VN-direct|Medium}:

- Incentivised sectors include science, technology and innovation (Art 15).
- Art 16 establishes the Investment Support Fund.
- Art 28 creates a special investment procedure for projects in high-tech zones and special economic zones, in which investor commitments replace technology appraisal and EIA-style steps.

## S9.13 Sandboxes

**Law on Science, Technology and Innovation 93/2025/QH15** (27 June 2025, effective 1 October 2025) [@REG-48; @REG2-13] {VN-direct|High}:

- Art 21 to 23 allow controlled testing of technologies, products and business models "not yet regulated or differing from current law".
- Art 21(1): the "*cơ quan nhà nước có thẩm quyền*" (competent state agency) permits testing. No single body is named.
- Art 21(3): the plan must set objectives, conditions and criteria for the technology or solution, risk management and participant protection.
- Duration: proposed by the firm, up to 3 years, extendable once by up to 3 years.
- Art 22: regulators and implementers are exempt from civil, administrative and criminal liability if they follow the rules, unless they knew or should have known of a risk and did not prevent it. Implementers remain liable to third parties.
- Art 21(6): the Government may issue detailed rules, including for sectors and for conflicts with other laws.
- Other articles: risk acceptance in R&D (Art 9); commercialisation, with at least 30% to creators where state funding is involved (Art 27 to 28); support for enterprise R&D (Art 34) [@REG-48] {VN-direct|High}.

**Implementing decrees.** Four decrees of 14 October 2025 guide the law: 263/2025 (autonomy, human resources, talent), 265/2025 (finance and investment), 267/2025 (programmes, tasks, research promotion) and 268/2025 (innovation tasks, loan interest support, vouchers, startups). Decree 268/2025 has no controlled-testing provisions, and we found no general sandbox decree [@REG2-14; @REG2-15] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**Resolution 193/2025/QH15** (19 February 2025; parts to 31 December 2030) is a pilot mechanism for science and technology. Its only controlled-testing item is low-earth-orbit satellite services (Art 13), so it is not usable for food [@REG-49] {VN-direct|High}.

## S9.15 Environment and carbon

- **Environmental impact assessment (EIA).** The Law on Environmental Protection 72/2020/QH14 is amended by Law 146/2025 from 1 January 2026. Decree 08/2022/ND-CP is amended by Decree 05/2025 (6 January 2025) and Decree 48/2026 (29 January 2026). Decree 48/2026 changes permit adjustment and phased EIA [@REG-58; @REG-43] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **The EIA gap.** The appendices with capacity thresholds for food, fermentation, feed and seafood processing (Appendices II to V) did not render in either wave. We can confirm only that Appendix II classifies activities by capacity (large, medium, small) and that Group I projects need an EIA. So we cannot say at what size a fermentation or feed plant needs a full EIA [@REG-58; @REG2-19] {VN-direct|Medium}. Decree 05/2025 moved some EIA appraisal and permitting to provinces from 6 January 2025 [@REG2-19] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Carbon market.** Decree 06/2022 as amended by Decree 119/2025 (9 June 2025) runs a pilot carbon market until the end of 2028, with full operation from 2029. Pilot quotas cover thermal power, steel and cement. Offsets can cover up to 30% of quotas, and Article 6.2 and 6.4 mechanisms are provided for. The extract says agriculture and food processing are not in the initial quota scope [@REG-59] {VN-direct|Medium}. Direct carbon revenue for alternative protein is unlikely before 2029, except through voluntary or Article 6 credits under an approved method. Whether any large food or feed facility is on the greenhouse gas inventory list is unresolved (DG-054).
- **Grid emissions.** The latest official grid emission factor, as of January 2026, is 0.6592 tCO2/MWh for 2023, published on 3 December 2024 [@COST-08; @COST-09] {VN-direct|High}. A power-intensive process in Vietnam carries a high Scope 2 footprint unless it buys renewable power.

## S9.16 Biodiversity, access and benefit sharing

- **Law on Biodiversity 20/2008/QH12**, amended by Law 146/2025/QH15 (effective 1 January 2026), adds a definition of gene-edited organisms and restructures Art 57: a permit is needed for foreign access, domestic commercial access and export of genetic resources [@REG-43; @REG-61] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Decree 59/2017/ND-CP** (12 May 2017) is still in force as amended, including by Decree 43/2026 (consolidated text 19/VBHN-BNNMT, 2026) [@REG-60; @REG-24] {VN-direct|High}. The points below are from the 2017 text and were not rechecked against the amendments:
  - Commercial research and product development need a licence (Art 7).
  - Registration is confirmed in 10 days. Non-commercial review takes 30 days. For commercial use, a council reviews within 90 days and a decision follows within 15 days.
  - A contract with the provider is certified by the commune People's Committee.
  - Benefit sharing is at least 1% of annual product revenue, or at least 2% of the value of an IP transfer (Art 22). The split is 30% to the provider and 70% to the state budget.
  - Derivatives are defined (Art 3(6)), and obligations pass on transfer (Art 14).
  - There is no provision on digital sequence information.
  - Microorganisms are not excluded, so microbes isolated from Vietnamese environments (for example from fermented foods or cassava waste) are in scope.
  - The licensing ministry is now MAE.
- **Practical point.** A startup that commercialises a strain isolated in Vietnam should budget for the licence and for benefit sharing of at least 1% of product revenue [@REG-60] {VN-direct|High}.

- **Law 131/2025/QH15** amending the IP Law (10 December 2025, effective 1 April 2026) adds rules on AI-created subject matter, a text and data mining exception, and non-physical industrial designs. Nothing on biotech exclusions was visible in the extract [@REG-62] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S9.20 How a new protein gets to market: a plain-language explainer

These are the routes as the law stood on 23 September 2026. They may change when the new Food Safety Law and its decree take effect; the National Assembly considers passage at its May 2027 session, so not before mid-2027 [@APR-07] {VN-direct|Medium}. Each step below is described in detail, with sources, in sections S9.3 to S9.13.

**1. Plant-based food from known ingredients** (tofu, textured soy, wheat gluten, jackfruit, *đồ chay*, plant milks).
Make it in a food-safe factory. Test the product at an accredited lab. File a self-declaration with the authority named by the province. You can sell right away [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}. We found no rule that stops you calling it *chay* or using words such as *sữa hạt* or *heo* with a qualifier, but do not mislead, and quantify any ingredient named in the product name [@REG2-24; @LBL-06] {VN-direct|Medium}. Print protein in the nutrition panel; a "high protein" claim needs 10 g per 100 g under the voluntary TCVN 14429:2025 [@LBL-02; @LBL-03] {VN-direct|High}. Because Vietnam has no mandatory allergen list, add soy and wheat warnings voluntarily. Many brands already use this route.

**2. Koji or other traditional mould fermentation on a food substrate** (*Aspergillus oryzae*, *Rhizopus*).
The route is the same as for plant-based food. The organisms have a long history of food use in Vietnam (*tương*, *nước tương*) and elsewhere, so legal risk is low [@REG-02] {VN-direct|Medium}. Keep strain identity and safety data on file. The science matters here: *A. oryzae* cannot make aflatoxin but can make cyclopiazonic acid, so use a characterised strain (see [[app-s13-science]]).

**3. Fungal biomass or mycoprotein food.**
Legally, the only route is the same self-declaration. There is no way to get the ingredient pre-approved [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}. If the fungus has no food history, an inspector could argue it is "not a food-type raw material" (Law Art 5(1)) or a "new-technology product not yet permitted" (Art 55(1)(c)) [@REG-01] {VN-direct|Medium}. Edible-mushroom species carry lower risk than new strains. Build a safety dossier and talk to VFA before launch.

**4. Microalgae food** (spirulina, chlorella).
Either self-declare as an ordinary food, or register as a health supplement at MOH (21 WD, GMP-certified factory) [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}. Newer algae species carry the same uncertainty as new fungi.

**5. Precision-fermented protein food.**
An imported ingredient can be self-declared, or is exempt from declaration if used only in your own production [@REG-02] {VN-direct|High}. Label it as GM if it is more than 5% of total ingredients, because a recombinant protein is probably a "product of a GMO"; whether an identical recombinant protein counts as "detectable", which would decide the label, is unsettled [@REG-02; @REG2-11; @LBL-10] {VN-direct|Medium}. If it works as an additive or enzyme not on the MOH list, register it with VFA (7 WD) [@REG-02; @REG-25] {VN-direct|High}. Making it in Vietnam with a GM microbe needs MAE's new closed-production certificate: Forms 32 and 33, a contained facility that prevents release, licensed waste treatment and OECD or G20 standards [@REG2-11] {VN-direct|High}. The decree gives about 60 WD for the certificate (5 + 50 + 5 WD); the fee is not published [@REG-24] {VN-direct|Medium}. No text says whether a GMO food-use certificate is also needed, so ask MAE and MOH in writing before investing.

**6. Cultivated meat or seafood.**
There is no national route. The law implies that new-technology food needs "permission to circulate", but there is no procedure to obtain it [@REG-01] {VN-direct|High}. Any genetically modified cell line adds GMO questions. The most concrete option is a supervised pilot in Hanoi's sandbox under the biotechnology field, with MOH consulted [@REG2-16; @REG2-17] {VN-direct|Medium}. Whether a city sandbox can set aside national food law is untested.

**7. Insect meal for livestock and poultry feed.**
Insects are on the permitted raw-material list, so no feeding trial is needed [@REG-32] {VN-direct|High}. You need a certified feed factory (province), a declared standard, conformity with the QCVN 01-190:2020 limits, and a label [@REG-29; @REG-36; @REG-41] {VN-direct|High}. Entobel has used this route since 2019 [@REG-44] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**8. Insect meal, yeast protein, duckweed or microalgae for shrimp and fish feed.**
None of these is on the aquafeed list as a raw material, because the list has no raw-material section. The Fisheries Law, read literally, requires a trial for any unlisted raw material [@REG2-01; @REG2-02] {VN-direct|High}. Practice evidently differs, because conventional feeds are sold without trials. Ask DFFI in writing whether your ingredient needs an aquafeed trial before you build a product on it.

**9. Duckweed or algae meal for livestock feed.**
*Bèo* (duckweed) and *tảo* (algae) are on the livestock list, so the route is the same as for insect meal [@REG-32] {VN-direct|High}. If grown on wastewater, test heavy metals and pathogens against QCVN 01-190:2020 [@REG-36] {VN-direct|High}.

**10. Yeast protein for livestock feed.**
Inactive yeasts, including Torula or Candida yeast and yeast grown on molasses, and by-products of amino-acid fermentation, have been on the livestock list since February 2023. The route is the same as for insect meal [@REG-33] {VN-direct|High}.

**11. Bacterial SCP or another new microbial protein for livestock feed.**
This is probably a "new substance". Run a feed trial under a DLPAH-approved protocol (15 + 5 WD to approve), then get the result recognised (15 + 5 WD). The material then enters the permitted list at the next annual update [@REG-29; @REG-32; @REG-34] {VN-direct|High}. Our estimate of the total is 6 to 18 months; that is an estimate, not a legal deadline. Do not sell it before it is listed: since 5 August 2026 the fine is VND 10 to 20 million per unlisted material, plus 1 to 3 months' suspension of feed production [@REG2-10] {VN-direct|High}.

**12. SCP for aquafeed.**
Register an aquafeed trial (20-day dossier appraisal), run it, and get the results recognised by the provincial People's Committee chair (10 WD). Importing trial material needs a provincial licence. Then declare the aquafeed products that contain it [@REG-37; @REG-38; @REG-41] {VN-direct|High}.

**13. A new food additive, enzyme or processing aid.**
Register the product declaration at VFA (7 WD), or ask MOH to amend the additive list with safety evidence [@REG-02; @REG-25] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S9.21 Foreign precedents and what Vietnam could copy

Full country comparisons are in [[app-s3-regional]]. This section covers only the regulatory mechanisms.

| Jurisdiction | Instrument | Mechanism | What Vietnam could copy by decree | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Singapore | Food Safety and Security Act (FSSA); FSSA (Authorisations: Administration) Regulations 2025 | Novel food means no history of food use for at least 20 years, including cell-cultured and precision-fermented products. Mandatory pre-market approval. Supplying an unapproved novel food has been an offence since 28 November 2025. The approved list (dated 14 August 2026) is published with self-assessment checklists for precision fermentation and biomass | Use the checklists as guidance for Vietnamese firms, and SFA approvals as a reliance reference | [@REG-63; @RGN-05] {VN-adjacent\|High} |
| Thailand | Ministry of Public Health Notification No. 376 (2016) and Thai FDA guidance | Pre-market safety assessment by FDA-recognised assessment units; FDA permission; separate forms for novel food, cultivated meat and "non-novel" foods; a mycoprotein guideline; an approved list updated in September 2026 (B.E. 2569). BIOTEC is the designated safety assessment unit for cultivated meat | Recognise Vietnamese institutes (for example the National Institute for Food Control) as assessment units; publish a positive list; add a "not novel" determination form | [@REG2-26; @RGN-32] {VN-adjacent\|Medium} |
| European Union | Regulation (EU) 2015/2283 | Novel means no significant consumption in the EU before 15 May 1997. Traditional foods from third countries can use a notification with an objection window. EFSA opinions show the questions a regulator asks, for example on manganese in duckweed powders | A "traditional food" fast lane for foods with a long history of use elsewhere (for example tempeh, koji products) | [@REG2-27; @SCI-28; @SCI-30] {general\|Low} |
| China | "New food raw material" approvals (National Health Commission) | 149 items approved by December 2023 (secondary source); first mycoprotein approval reported in 2025 | A public, growing positive list | [@REG2-27; @RGN-20] {general\|Medium} |
| South Korea | Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) temporary standards under the Food Sanitation Act; Food Tech Industry Promotion Act | A firm can apply for a temporary standard for an ingredient not in the Food Code; extended to cell-cultured ingredients, with applications open since February 2024; a fee of KRW 45 million and review of up to 270 WD, as reported in February 2024; existing instruments were amended in about nine months (our calculation, May 2023 to February 2024) | A firm-initiated "temporary standard" path inside the new implementing decree, with a published fee and review time | [@RGN-19; @RGN-21; @RGN-34] {VN-adjacent\|Medium} |
| Vietnam (own model) | Decree 43/2026 GMO fast track | 17 WD of council review if at least 5 developed OECD or G20 countries approved the event | A reliance lane: faster review for new foods approved by 2 or more reference regulators | [@REG-18; @REG-23] {VN-direct\|High} |
| Codex, ASEAN | Codex work on new food sources and production systems; ASEAN food safety bodies | Not verified in this study | None yet | Gap |

Three lessons from the regional record [@RGN-19; @RGN-21; @RGN-32] {VN-adjacent|Medium}:

- **Korea shows a route that does not need a new law.** A safety-assessment step can be added inside an existing instrument, with a published fee and review time.
- **Thailand shows how to borrow assessors.** An existing science body can be designated as the assessment unit instead of building a new agency.
- **A framework is not enough.** Thailand and Korea have routes but had no cultivated-meat approval by September 2026. Staff capacity and statutory timelines matter as much as the legal text.

## S9.22 Policy options

This table shows the first 25 rows of `policy_options.csv`: 11 options ranked by the wave 2 regulation review and 14 options from wave 1. The file now has 33 rows; options PO-026 to PO-033, added by the synthesis, are ranked and explained in [[ch27-policy-options]]. The wave 2 ranking multiplies impact on investability by feasibility and time-criticality. Effort: Low = a letter, guidance or list update; Medium = a circular or decree amendment; High = a new law chapter or regime. [[ch27-policy-options]] discusses them.

data.title: S10. Administrative map after the 2025 reforms
data.summary: The 34 provincial-level units that replaced Vietnam's 63 on 1 July 2025, where the alternative-protein clusters now sit, the end of the district tier, the 2025 ministry mergers, and practical rules for reading older statistics and addresses.
data.body:
# S10. Administrative map after the 2025 reforms

Vietnam redrew its provincial map and merged several ministries in 2025. Every location and agency name in this report uses the new map and the new names. This appendix is the reference for doing so. It is built from `provinces.csv` (34 rows) and `ministries.csv` (6 rows).

> **Method note.** The provincial list, the former units, area and population are taken from Resolution 202/2025/QH15 itself. The former unit that hosts each new administrative centre comes from Party Resolution 60-NQ/TW. The ward names of the centres come from English Wikipedia, because the resolutions name only the former province [@GT-01; @GT-02; @GT-03] {VN-direct|High}. Area and population are the Government dossier figures stated in the resolution; the resolution does not state their reference date.

## S10.1 What changed, and when

| Date | Change | Instrument | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18 Feb 2025 | Government restructured to 14 ministries and 3 ministerial-level agencies, operating from 1 March 2025 | Resolution 176/2025/QH15 | [@GT-04] {VN-direct\|High} |
| 12 Apr 2025 | Party decision on the provincial mergers and the location of each new political-administrative centre; district-level units to end; commune-level units to be cut by 60 to 70% | Resolution 60-NQ/TW | [@GT-02] {VN-direct\|High} |
| 12 Jun 2025 | National Assembly resolution: 23 merger clauses covering 52 former units, and 11 units unchanged | Resolution 202/2025/QH15 | [@GT-01] {VN-direct\|High} |
| 1 Jul 2025 | The 34 new provincial authorities "officially operate"; the district tier ends; local government has two tiers, province and commune | Resolution 202/2025/QH15 Art 2; Resolution 60-NQ/TW | [@GT-01; @GT-02] {VN-direct\|High} |

The result is 34 provincial-level units: 28 provinces and 6 centrally governed cities (Hanoi, Hue, Hai Phong, Da Nang, Ho Chi Minh City and Can Tho) [@GT-01] {VN-direct|High}. The 11 unchanged units are Hanoi, Hue, Cao Bang, Dien Bien, Ha Tinh, Lai Chau, Lang Son, Nghe An, Quang Ninh, Thanh Hoa and Son La [@GT-01] {VN-direct|High}. We did not verify the final number of communes.

> **Correction.** Earlier drafts placed Long An inside Ho Chi Minh City. Resolution 202/2025/QH15 Art 1(18) merges Long An into **Tay Ninh**, whose centre is in former Long An. Binh Duong and Ba Ria-Vung Tau did merge into Ho Chi Minh City, and Binh Phuoc into Dong Nai [@GT-01; @GT-02] {VN-direct|High}. ## S10.5 The end of the district tier

- From 1 July 2025, local government has two tiers: province and commune (including wards). District-level units no longer exist [@GT-02] {VN-direct|High}.
- Addresses now read "ward or commune, province". For example, Entobel's plant is at Lot 05, Street N3, Dat Do I Industrial Zone, Dat Do commune, Ho Chi Minh City [@REG-44] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Licensing moved to provincial chairs. Many feed and aquafeed procedures now sit with provincial People's Committee chairs: feed factory certificates, supplement-feed appraisal, import licences for unpublished feed, aquafeed trial recognition and import licences for unlisted aquafeed [@REG-41; @REG-35] {VN-direct|High}. Expect provincial officials, not district officials, to handle them. See [[app-s9-regulation]].
- The number and date of the Law on Organisation of Local Government that sets the two-tier model were not verified [@GT-02] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## S10.6 Ministries after the 2025 restructuring

From `ministries.csv`. All took effect on 1 March 2025, except the provincial row (1 July 2025).

| ID | Ministry now | Vietnamese name | Predecessors | Legal basis | Units relevant to alternative protein | Roles | Evidence |

| MIN-002 | Ministry of Science and Technology (MOST) | *Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ* | MOST and the Ministry of Information and Communications | Resolution 176/2025/QH15; Decree 55/2025/ND-CP (2 Mar 2025) | Department of Science and Technology; Department of Technology Assessment and Appraisal; Bureau of Intellectual Property; National Committee for Standards, Metrology and Quality; Bureau of Digital Transformation | Science law and sandbox; high-tech and strategic technology lists; national standards; IP; halal certifier registration | [@GT-04; @GT-06; @REG-48; @REG-27] {VN-direct\|High} |
| MIN-003 | Ministry of Finance (MOF) | *Bộ Tài chính* | MOF and the Ministry of Planning and Investment | Resolution 176/2025/QH15; Decree 29/2025/ND-CP (24 Feb 2025), amended by Decree 166/2025/ND-CP (30 Jun 2025) | Tax departments; investment and enterprise units (former MPI); national statistics | Corporate income tax incentives; investment law; Investment Support Fund; customs and tariffs; statistics | [@GT-04; @GT-07] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| MIN-004 | Ministry of Industry and Trade (MOIT) | *Bộ Công Thương* | Name unchanged | Resolution 176/2025/QH15; Decree 40/2025/ND-CP (26 Feb 2025) | Unit list not read | Biofuel (E10) roadmap; power plan; food safety for some processed products until the new Food Safety Law | [@GT-04; @GT-08; @GT-10] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| MIN-005 | Ministry of Health (MOH) | *Bộ Y tế* | Name unchanged | Resolution 176/2025/QH15; Decree 42/2025/ND-CP (27 Feb 2025) | Food Safety Department (Vietnam Food Administration, VFA); National Institute for Food Control | Food Safety Law and Decree 15/2018; lead drafter of the revised law; additives; health supplements | [@GT-04; @GT-09; @REG-08; @REG-02; @IND-61] {VN-direct\|Medium} |
| MIN-006 | Provincial People's Committees (34 units) | *Ủy ban nhân dân cấp tỉnh* | 63 provincial units before 1 Jul 2025 | Resolution 202/2025/QH15; Decree 136/2025 (decentralisation) | Provincial Departments of Agriculture and Environment, Science and Technology, Health, and Industry and Trade | Many feed and aquafeed procedures; investment registration; EIA for smaller projects | [@GT-01; @GT-03; @REG-41] {VN-direct\|Medium} |

- The unit lists for MOF, MOIT and MOH were not read; only titles and dates are confirmed [@GT-07; @GT-08; @GT-09] {VN-direct|Medium}. The MAE unit list comes from the wave 1 reading of Decree 35/2025 [@REG-42] {VN-direct|High}.
- Livestock production and veterinary services were merged into one MAE department [@REG-42] {VN-direct|High}.
- One ministry (MAE) now holds feed, aquafeed, GMO biosafety, genetic resources and carbon, and one (MOST) holds standards, the sandbox, high-tech status and IP [@GT-04; @GT-06; @REG-42; @REG-48] {VN-direct|High}.

## S10.7 Practical rules for reading pre-2025 statistics and addresses

1. **Name the new unit first.** Write "Tay Ninh (former Long An)" or "Ho Chi Minh City (former Ba Ria-Vung Tau)" on first use in a page. Use the former name alone only when quoting a historical document.
2. **Re-aggregate before comparing.** Provincial statistics before July 2025 use the 63-unit map. To compare them with later data, add up the former units listed in the `former_units` column of `provinces.csv`. Do not compare a pre-2025 "Tay Ninh" figure with a post-2025 one: the new unit also contains former Long An. We expect official series from 2025 onward to use the 34-unit map but did not verify this.
3. **Watch the split-name units.** In the seven units in section S10.3, the provincial offices sit in a different former province from the one that gave the unit its name.
4. **Drop districts from addresses.** Older addresses that name a district are correct for historical documents but should be converted to "ward or commune, province" for current licences and contracts.
5. **Map facilities through their former province.** An industrial zone, plant or port keeps its own name; look up its former province, then read the new unit from `provinces.csv`. In the report's data files, the `province_current` and `province_former` columns were filled this way and left blank where a location was vague or ambiguous.
6. **Expect some bodies to keep old names.** Some utilities and firms still publish under former provincial names; for example, BIWASE still publishes its own water tariff for former Binh Duong, now part of Ho Chi Minh City [@COST-12; @GT-01] {VN-direct|Medium}.
7. **Use the new ministry names.** Write MAE, MOST, MOF, MOIT and MOH for anything after 1 March 2025, and "MARD (now MAE)" for older documents [@GT-04] {VN-direct|High}.
8. **Mind the population sources.** Resolution 202 gives dossier figures with no stated reference date; the statistics office and the UN give national totals that differ by about 0.7 million for 2025 (see [[app-f1-outlook]]) [@GT-01; @MAC-19; @GT-12] {VN-direct|Medium}.

## Gaps and how to close them

| # | Gap | Cheapest way to close it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Final number of commune-level units after 1 July 2025 | National Assembly Standing Committee resolutions on each province's commune reorganisation (June 2025), or the Ministry of Home Affairs |
| 2 | Number and date of the Law on Organisation of Local Government 2025 | Search thuvienphapluat.vn for "Luật Tổ chức chính quyền địa phương 2025" |
| 3 | Unit lists of MOF, MOIT and MOH after March 2025, and which MOIT unit keeps food-safety duties until the new Food Safety Law | Read Decrees 29/2025, 40/2025 and 42/2025 |
| 4 | Whether ward names of centres (for example Long An ward, Tran Bien ward) match current company registrations | The National Business Registration Portal |
| 5 | A 63-to-34 crosswalk for official provincial series (livestock herds, aquaculture output, cassava area) | Build from `provinces.csv` `former_units` and statistics office tables |
| 6 | Provincial shares of shrimp, pangasius and cassava output on the new map | Statistics office provincial tables, re-aggregated |

## Related data files

- `provinces.csv`: the 34 units with type, administrative centre, former units, area and population (section S10.2).
- `ministries.csv`: the six ministry and provincial rows (section S10.6).
- `facilities.csv`, `feedstocks.csv` and `companies.csv`: carry `province_current` and `province_former` columns mapped with `provinces.csv` (see [[app-s5-facilities]], [[app-s4-feedstocks]] and [[app-s1-directory]]).
- `disagreements.csv`: DG-123 and DG-124 (see [[app-r2-disagreements]]).
- Working paper: `working-papers/wave2/geo_time/geo_time.md`.

data.title: S11. Capital: deals, investors and funding programmes
data.summary: Every disclosed alternative-protein and adjacent agrifood deal linked to Vietnam, the size of Vietnamese venture and private equity markets, the Entobel financing template, global and regional investment trends, development finance, the new state venture funds, grants open in 2026, accelerators and exit routes.
data.body:
# S11. Capital: deals, investors and funding programmes

This appendix sets out the money side of Vietnamese alternative protein: the deals that have happened, the investors with a relevant track record, the size of the local venture and private equity (PE) market, development finance institutions (DFIs), the state venture framework created in 2025 and 2026, grants and philanthropy, accelerators, and exit routes. It focuses on money for supply: ingredient, feed and processing plants, pilot facilities and research.

Coverage warning. The web-search cap for the capital research was reached early; after that only direct reads of known pages were possible. DFIs beyond IFC, Proparco and ADB Ventures, regional strategic venture arms, Vietnamese food M&A, aquaculture-tech and feed-tech deals, and H1 2026 Vietnam venture totals are therefore incomplete. Absence of a deal here means "not found", not "does not exist".

Currency. Amounts are given as reported. Where we convert VND to USD, we use VND 26,000 per USD (our calculation); the capital research used about VND 25,380 per USD, implied by a March 2026 press report [@CAP-32] {VN-direct|Medium}, so some source USD figures differ slightly from ours.

## S11.1 Key findings

1. **Disclosed venture money into Vietnam-based alternative protein is small and concentrated in one insect company.** Entobel's USD 32.5 million project financing (2022 to 2023) is the only disclosed round above USD 5 million we found from 2015 to September 2026 [@CAP-01; @CAP-02; @CAP-04] {VN-direct|Medium}.
2. **We found no disclosed venture round for any Vietnam-based plant-based meat, plant-based dairy, precision fermentation, microalgae or cultivated-meat company.** The only plant-protein fundraising found is Emmay's: about USD 250,000 from three angel rounds, plus two US grants of unstated size, by 2021 (company claim) [@CAP-15] {VN-direct|Low}.
3. **Vietnamese strategic money has gone outward.** Vinh Hoan invested in Shiok Meats and Avant Meats (cultivated seafood, 2021); VinaCapital Ventures invested in Korea's INNOHAS (plant-based meat, 2024) [@CAP-16; @CAP-17; @CAP-18] {VN-direct|Low}.
4. **Vietnamese venture capital was USD 509 million in 103 deals in 2025; agriculture got USD 1 million, about 0.2%** (our calculation: 1 / 509) [@CAP-21] {VN-direct|Medium}. Private equity reached a record USD 3.96 billion in 46 deals [@CAP-21; @CAP-22] {VN-direct|Medium}.
5. **There were no VC- or PE-backed technology IPOs in 2025 or the four years before**, so a realistic exit for a food or ingredient company is a trade sale or a PE buyout [@CAP-21; @CAP-22] {VN-direct|Medium}.
6. **A state venture framework now exists.** Decree 264/2025/ND-CP (in force 14 October 2025) allows national and provincial venture funds to accept up to 50% portfolio loss per investment cycle. Ho Chi Minh City's fund (VND 500 bn) plans its first investments in Q4 2026; Hanoi's (VND 230 bn) caps each investment at 5% of the fund, about USD 0.44 million (our calculation at VND 26,000 per USD) [@CAP-29; @CAP-33; @CAP-34] {VN-direct|Medium}.
7. **Global alternative-protein investment is at a cyclical low and has shifted towards fermentation:** USD 881 million in 2025 and USD 359 million in H1 2026 [@CAP-51] {general|High}.
8. **IFC is the only DFI we found with a direct Vietnamese alternative-protein ticket** (Entobel, USD 2.5 million). Its other Vietnamese tickets found run from USD 20 million (GS25, retail) to USD 90.6 million (Mavin, proposed) [@VCO-20; @CAP-41; @CAP-44] {VN-direct|Medium}.
9. **The largest alternative-protein R&D call we found open to Vietnamese applicants in 2026 has closed.** Coefficient Giving's RFP (up to USD 30 million) closed its two rounds on 10 August and 15 September 2026 [@CAP-57] {general|High}.

## S11.2 Deal log

Readings:

- **Only insects have attracted disclosed venture money in Vietnam.** Cricket One's three rounds were undisclosed or described only as "seven-figure" (for the pre-Series A, Corecam's own commitment) [@CAP-11; @CAP-12; @CAP-13] {VN-direct|Medium}.

We found no disclosed deals for Vietnamese aquaculture-tech, feed-tech (other than insects), microalgae, plant-based dairy or agrifood biotech startups. This is a coverage gap, not evidence of absence.

In v0.6 the template list below also gave Mekong's typical ticket range as USD 5 million to 25 million; the cited sources show only the USD 25 million Entobel ticket.

What the template implies for a Vietnamese feed or ingredient plant (our reading):

- a local PE lead able to write a ticket of about USD 25 million, as Mekong did for Entobel, with a local co-investor [@CAP-01; @CAP-02] {VN-direct|Medium};
- a small DFI "upstream" ticket that de-risks the first plant;
- a strategic offtake with a seafood exporter or feed major signed before or alongside the plant;
- a Singapore holding company, as Entobel used;
- a path to USD 20 million or more of capex, the capital research's judgement from Entobel's USD 32.5 million project cost [@CAP-04] {VN-direct|Low}. Few Vietnamese alternative-protein companies can show that today.

## S11.8 State venture framework and state finance

**Decree 264/2025/ND-CP on national and local venture funds** (signed and in force 14 October 2025) [@CAP-29; @CAP-30] {VN-direct|High}:

- National fund: MOST represents the state's capital; at least VND 500 bn from the development budget at the start (about USD 19 million); at least VND 2,000 bn within five years including mobilised capital (about USD 77 million) (USD figures: our calculation).
- Investment forms: direct equity, fund-of-funds, co-investment.
- Loss threshold: 50% of charter capital across the portfolio per investment cycle (Art. 10.4.a).
- Cycle: 10 years, or 15 for strategic or dual-use technology (Art. 10.1.c).
- Managers are exempt from liability for losses from "objective risks" (Art. 14).
- Priority sectors include the green and circular economy (Art. 5.3).
- Local funds invest only in Vietnam; the provincial People's Committee sets the state share.
- Status: in June 2026 MOST was still preparing the national fund proposal; experts and international fund representatives quoted in the press favoured a fund-of-funds model [@CAP-31] {VN-direct|Medium}.

Ho Chi Minh City hosts over half of Vietnam's startups and about half of its VC funds [@CAP-36] {VN-direct|Medium}.

**NATIF (National Technology Innovation Fund, under MOST).** Reorganised under Decree 77/2026/ND-CP (17 March 2026); it funds technology innovation, intellectual property, startups and interest subsidies [@CAP-37] {VN-direct|Medium}. The 2026 Round 1 interest subsidy had a VND 50 bn budget (about USD 1.9 million, our calculation); it covered 50% of loan interest, capped at 6% a year, for up to five years; borrowers needed a bank credit contract with at least 12 months left and the capacity to repay, and those with a profit in the last year and no bad debt in 24 months got priority; partner banks included VPBank and BIDV; the deadline was 20 September 2026 [@CAP-38] {VN-direct|Medium}. It suits established manufacturers adding a line, not pre-revenue startups.

**Credit programmes.**

- A bank-funded preferential programme of VND 500 trillion (2025 to 2030; VND 100 trillion in 2025 to 2026) covers strategic infrastructure, high technology and innovation through 21 banks; no agriculture-specific window was found [@CAP-40] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- Decree 156/2025 (in force 1 July 2025) raises unsecured lending limits for agriculture (for example up to VND 5 bn for cooperatives) and gives organic and circular agriculture the same credit treatment as high-tech agriculture [@CAP-39] {VN-direct|Medium}. A side-stream protein plant framed as circular agriculture might qualify; this has not been tested.

**Other state instruments** covered elsewhere: the Investment Support Fund under Decree 182/2024 (high thresholds; see [[app-s9-regulation]]) [@REG-46] {VN-direct|High}; specialised science funds with state capital under Law 93/2025/QH15 ([[app-s7-research]]) [@REG-48] {VN-direct|High}; and interest subsidies of 70% of the loan interest rate, capped at 8% a year, in hi-tech agriculture zones under Decree 263/2026 [@INF-23] {VN-direct|Medium} ([[app-s8-labs-talent]]).

## S11.11 Exit landscape

- **IPO route: closed for technology.** Vietnam had three IPOs in 2025, all in financial services (USD 1.35 billion), and no VC- or PE-backed technology IPOs in 2025 or the four years before; the IPO pipeline is expected to reach USD 3 billion to 5 billion in 2026 to 2027 [@CAP-21; @CAP-22] {VN-direct|Medium}.
- **Revealed strategic interest (verified):** Vinh Hoan (cultivated seafood stakes; insect meal buyer), CJ CheilJedang (co-investor in Shiok; large Vietnamese food footprint), VinaCapital (market-entry partner for INNOHAS) [@CAP-16; @CAP-17; @CAP-18; @ECO-05] {VN-direct|Low}.
- **Plausible acquirers by fit (not verified as interested):** Masan (consumer foods, meat), Vinamilk, TH, Nutifood and Vinasoy/QNS (plant milks), KIDO (edible oils and fats), C.P. Vietnam, De Heus and other feed majors (feed ingredients), Thai Union, Minh Phu and Vinh Hoan (aquafeed and seafood), Ajinomoto and Vedan (fermentation). This list comes from sector logic, not deal evidence.
- **Multiples:** M&A multiples for Vietnamese food deals were not established. No Vietnamese alternative-protein company has had a disclosed exit.
- **Consolidation among buyers:** De Heus Vietnam lists 21 plants (September 2026) and completed its purchase of CJ Feed & Care in March 2026, which (our reading) concentrates feed buying power in one strategic; whether the 21 plants include the former CJ mills is not known [@VCO-09; @VCO-08] {VN-direct|Medium}.

> **For investors.** A thesis in Vietnamese alternative protein has to rest on B2B feed or ingredient revenue and a strategic buyer, not on a consumer-brand exit. Agriculture VC was about USD 1 million in 2025 [@CAP-21] {VN-direct|Medium}, and there is no track record of venture exits.
